fullText:
UNITED NATIONS (AP) — The heads of major artificial intelligence firms pleaded with the United Nations on Wednesday to set controls over the burgeoning technology they are designing in order to save the world — or, at least, its people.

"If managed poorly, I even believe AI could be a risk to humanity as a whole," said Dario Amodei, the chief executive officer of Anthropic.

"We could lose control of the future to AI," said his competitor, Sam Altman, CEO of OpenAI.

Both said the countries of the world, though the U.N. Security Council, where they testified Wednesday afternoon, have to set safeguards, which would be actual controls to prevent the technology from getting too powerful to rein in. They also called for the world to make sure that the power of AI isn't concentrated in one company or country.

For world leaders, one key question about AI is this: Who should control life-and-death decisions — human or machine?

The United Nations Security Council on Wednesday huddled with top technology leaders to figure out if the increasing abilities and pervasiveness of artificial intelligence should be controlled and, if so, by who. Other lingering questions: How could it be done? When might it be just too late?

The day before, U.N. Secretary-General Antonio Guterres warned of "killer robots." Experts and European leaders said that's not hyperbole but something that's already a reality or at least perilously close.

title: How state errors mistakenly put more than 30,000 noncitizens on voter rolls
description:
US states may have added more than 30,000 self-declared non-citizens to the nation’s voter rolls since 2000 because of software glitches and clerical errors made while processing their driver's license and state ID applications, according to official records reviewed by Reuters. 
   The cases expose weaknesses in voter registration systems across a dozen US states governed by both Democrats and Republicans, but at numbers that experts said were too small relative to the country’s more than 170 million registered voters to impact elections. Reuters was not ‌able to determine how many of these non-citizens actually cast a ballot. 
   The findings suggest that inadvertent bureaucratic failures, rather than organized efforts to register immigrants illegally, are a major source of non-citizen registrations, and raise questions about whether legislative efforts to require proof of citizenship for voter registration ‌would eliminate the issue. 
   President Donald Trump and his supporters have claimed, without evidence, that non-citizen voting is widespread and part of an organized conspiracy led by Democrats who hope to retake Congress in November's midterm elections, and are pushing lawmakers to toughen up voting requirements.
fullText:
WASHINGTON, Sept 23 (Reuters) - US states may have added more than 30,000 self-declared non-citizens to the nation's voter rolls since 2000 because of software glitches and clerical errors made while processing their driver's license and state ID applications, according to official records reviewed by Reuters.

The cases expose weaknesses in voter registration systems across a dozen US states governed by both Democrats and Republicans, but at numbers that experts said were too small relative to the country's more than 170 million registered voters to impact elections. Reuters was not ‌able to determine how many of these non-citizens actually cast a ballot.

The findings suggest that inadvertent bureaucratic failures, rather than organized efforts to register immigrants illegally, are a major source of non-citizen registrations, and raise questions about whether legislative efforts to require proof of citizenship for voter registration ‌would eliminate the issue.

President Donald Trump and his supporters have claimed, without evidence, that non-citizen voting is widespread and part of an organized conspiracy led by Democrats who hope to retake Congress in November's midterm elections, and are pushing lawmakers to toughen up voting requirements.

New Jersey announced the most recent high-profile case of errant voter registrations over the summer, saying a technology glitch added about 6,600 non-citizens ​to voter rolls between June 2023 and June 2024, even though they answered "no" when asked if they were citizens while applying for licenses and IDs.

Bureaucratic errors have also been reported in at least 11 other states – including Republican strongholds like Iowa, Texas and South Dakota - bringing the nationwide figure above 30,000 since 2000, according to the Reuters reporting.

A nationwide tally of such mistakes has not previously been reported.

The data showed errors occurred in California, Illinois, Iowa, Nevada, Ohio, Oregon, Pennsylvania, South Dakota, Texas, Utah and Virginia.

The numbers are inexact because state data is often tentative and subject to revision.

Such mistakes are likely a top reason non-citizens make it onto the nation's voter rolls, according to Don Palmer, a senior legal fellow for election integrity at the conservative Heritage Foundation and former Trump-appointed ‌chair of the US Election Assistance Commission.

"I think that's the primary issue," Palmer said. "Driver's license agencies often make mistakes, ⁠and they often are not taking this as seriously as election officials." He said states also need to do more to verify voter eligibility.

The White House has pressured Congress to pass the SAVE America Act, a proposal to crack down on illegal voting that would require people to show proof of US citizenship to register to vote, and a photo ID to cast a ballot.

But it is unlikely such a bill would prevent the kinds of mistakes being made by state agencies, said David Becker, executive ⁠director of CEIR.

"In each of these instances, the individual did exactly what they were supposed to do. If there was some requirement that you had to show proof of citizenship, these problems would still exist, because the processes themselves failed," he said.

Proponents of the SAVE America Act say it is a common-sense way to ensure only eligible voters can cast ballots. Most states don't require documented proof of citizenship.

Critics counter that the legislation's restrictions could disenfranchise millions of voters who lack easy access to passports or birth certificates, including low-income people and racial minorities, while creating unnecessary turmoil for the Nov. 3 midterm elections.

"This is not a problem," said Elaine Kamarck, an expert on governance at the Brookings Institution. "There's just no evidence that ​massive ​numbers of non-citizens are voting."

Immigrants do sometimes make false declarations about their citizenship in order to be registered to vote in US elections, according to the Department of Justice. But there ​is no evidence to show it is widespread.

A Reuters data analysis published earlier this year showed federal prosecutors have charged ‌only 129 people under a federal "voting by aliens" statute created by Congress in 1996. In none of those cases did prosecutors allege a coordinated effort to influence an election.

The White House said non-citizen voter registrations were proof that US elections have been compromised and cited 11 arrests of non-citizens for illegal voting announced by federal authorities since May.

"The real story here is after decades of the media denying that non-citizens register and vote in our elections, they are finally being forced to admit after a flurry of recent arrests nationwide that it does happen," White House spokesperson Lauren Bis said in a statement.

Underlying the glitches and human errors are state motor-voter systems that register people to vote when they apply for driver's licenses, state IDs and other government services under the National Voter Registration Act.

The largely Democratic initiative to address low voter participation passed in 1993 with bipartisan support under then-President Bill Clinton. Voter registration has climbed to more than 86% in 2024, from 62% in 1990, according to Census data and the US Election Assistance Commission.

Republicans claim that such state motor-voter systems have become a major problem, however, due to the doubling of the US immigrant population since 1990.

Automatically registering people to vote in this way "is irrational when you realize people that are not citizens in the United States are getting ‌driver's licenses," said US Representative Bryan Steil, a Wisconsin Republican who oversees federal election policy as chair of the House Administration Committee.

All 50 states allow legal immigrants to obtain driver's ​licenses, while 19 US states and the District of Columbia also provide driver's licenses to undocumented immigrants.

FOREIGN PASSPORTS, BIRTH CERTIFICATES

Randall Marquis, a Canadian who lives in California, remembers the day when he got ​a card in the mail notifying him that he was registered to vote in the 2018 midterm elections during Trump's first term.

"I just said, 'Well, this ​is stupid.' So, I put it aside. But after thinking about it, I decided, no, it's more than stupid. This is bad!"  the 71-year-old green card holder told Reuters.

He alerted news organizations, and state officials later disclosed that as many as 1,500 non-citizens had ‌been mistakenly registered to vote by the California Department of Motor Vehicles due to a processing error, according to media ​reports.

State officials did not respond to Reuters queries seeking confirmation.

Similar problems have happened in ​Oregon where hundreds of immigrants who presented foreign passports and birth certificates were registered to vote because of clerical mistakes at the Department of Motor Vehicles, according to state records.

DMV officials also registered hundreds of American Samoans who presented US passports, not realizing that people from the US territory are nationals but not citizens, and therefore not eligible to vote.

In some other states, estimates of registered non-citizens have been initially overstated.

Just before the 2024 election, Iowa, for example, announced that more than 2,000 people had registered to vote or had voted in the state after self-reporting to the Iowa ​Department of Transportation as non-citizens.

Six months later, the number shrank to 277.

Iowa state officials said 35 non-citizens cast ballots that ‌were counted in the 2024 general election. Overall, more than 1.6 million Iowans voted in that election.

The problems are bigger elsewhere. Since 2014, Virginia has reported hundreds of non-citizens each year on its voter rolls who identified themselves as foreign nationals, with a total of more ​than 4,500 in 2025 alone, according to annual reports by the state Department of Elections.

State officials say those numbers include people who later became citizens, and others who were stricken off the rolls.

Palmer of the Heritage Foundation said states should be required to address the issue.

"There's ​an obligation to fix the problem. So, take the politics out, and fix the problem," he said.

title: Judge weighs White House ban on 3 news outlets but issues no immediate ruling
description:
— A judge heard arguments Wednesday but did not rule from the bench in a case on President Donald Trump’s ban of three news outlets from White House grounds. 
The hearing marked the latest development in an extraordinary showdown between Trump and media outlets whose coverage he dislikes. Trump banned CNN, MS NOW and Politico beginning Friday, assailing what he called “fake news.” More recently the president has said negative coverage was dangerous for the country. The outlets argued they were singled out because of the content of their coverage — in other words, viewpoint discrimination and called the ban a “blatant violation” of the First Amendment.
fullText:
WASHINGTON (AP) — A judge heard arguments Wednesday but did not rule from the bench in a case on President Donald Trump's ban of three news outlets from White House grounds.

The hearing marked the latest development in an extraordinary showdown between Trump and media outlets whose coverage he dislikes. Trump banned CNN, MS NOW and Politico beginning Friday, assailing what he called "fake news." More recently the president has said negative coverage was dangerous for the country. The outlets argued they were singled out because of the content of their coverage — in other words, viewpoint discrimination and called the ban a "blatant violation" of the First Amendment.

U.S. District Judge Timothy Kelly — whom Trump nominated in 2017 and who ordered a CNN journalist's access restored in a similar case in 2018 — didn't immediately rule on the news outlets' request for a restraining order. It was unclear when he would issue a decision.

He opened by reminding both sides that he's required to apply case precedent.

The rulings in two prior cases over press access — including one that went to the U.S. Supreme Court — made clear that journalists were entitled to an opportunity to be heard before they have their press passes revoked.

Justice Department attorney Michael Velchik has argued that the rulings in the earlier cases were wrong.

"Maybe they were, maybe they weren't, but currently as a district judge I have to apply them," Kelly said.

Arguments began with Theodore Boutrous Jr., attorney for the outlets, calling the ban an "unprecedented, unreasonable punishment" and saying there was "not a semblance of due process."

Velchik told the court that "access to the White House is a privilege, not a right."

"The president should be able to take immediate action to protect national security," he added.

The administration has doubled down on its contention that it has the right to decide who can set foot in the White House.

In filing late Tuesday, administration lawyers argued that the ban does not violate the First Amendment, which guarantees the right to a free press. It contended that the outlets, in their reporting, violated "standards of professionalism and decorum expected of those given access to the White House complex, including by trafficking in verifiable falsehoods about national security and other issues and publishing sensitive or classified information."

The administration went on to detail letters that were sent to each outlet that identified "a non-exhaustive list of reporting incidents, including those that have threatened national security and spread falsehoods."

The "reporting incidents" cited in the filing included: CNN reporting on "'top-secret' construction details related to the East Wing bunker"; MS NOW reporting "on an alleged leak investigation"; and Politico publishing "a document detailing funding for the White House ballroom containing intricate descriptions of how the Secret Service would invest in security improvements."

Further examples were given in individual letters. Politico's letter detailed six incidents of reporting, including in June citing a "senior administration official … granted anonymity" predicting whether a preliminary deal would end the conflict with Iran.

That item appeared to reference a background briefing set up by the White House, where an official briefed reporters on condition of anonymity under ground rules set by the White House itself. Several other outlets also reported the official's remarks.

Trump began to emphasize the national security argument Tuesday, when he said negative coverage was dangerous for the country.

"I think we have a right to clean out fake news," he told reporters at the United Nations, defending the ban, which was suddenly announced Friday. The next day, journalists for the three outlets arrived at work to find their entry badges disabled.

The ban prompted other media outlets to take action in solidarity. The five-network U.S. network press pool — a rotating cast of news outlets that covers the president, and to which CNN belongs — decided to suspend coverage of Trump events until further notice. The Associated Press joined a group of organizations that refrained from publishing photos of the president Monday. On Wednesday, the network pool was again missing from a daily White House press schedule.

The ban and subsequent lawsuit are part of a long-running conflict between the president — especially in his second term — and media outlets he finds unfavorable. Trump has responded in the courtroom, or with regulatory action. He's also lashed out at individual reporters in personal terms.

An amicus brief was filed by other news groups Wednesday, urging the court to immediately restore the three outlets' White House access.

The brief — filed by the Reporters Committee for Freedom of the Press, the White House Correspondents' Association and 49 media outlets and industry groups, including The Associated Press, The New York Times and Reuters — says "the targeted expulsion of news media from White House grounds injures the public interest" and that "unassailable First Amendment law makes any viewpoint-based decision to bar reporters from a nonpublic forum constitutionally repugnant."

The proceedings are historic, said Katie Fallow, deputy litigation director at the Knight First Amendment Institute at Columbia University.

"No president has taken this explicit of a step" to ban entire news outlets because he doesn't like their reporting, she said. "There have been various presidents throughout history who have grumbled about the press or threatened to take more major steps, but really there was nothing at this level before Trump."

Noveck reported from New York. Associated Press journalist Laurie Kellman contributed from London.

title: Iran's president backs diplomacy but rules out surrender after Trump’s threat
fullText:
President Masoud Pezeshkian has said Iran will never "bend the knee" after almost seven months of war with the US and Israel, but is ready for a diplomatic solution to the conflict.

Responding to US President Donald Trump's threat to "annihilate" the Islamic Republic if a deal is not reached soon, he told the UN General Assembly: "The resistance of the Iranian people will only increase in the face of sanctions, increased pressure, increased bullying."

Pezeshkian also insisted any deal would have to include an end to the US blockade stopping Iranian ships from using a key Gulf waterway.

"It cannot be the case that everyone benefits from the Strait of Hormuz while we are denied access," he said.

There was no immediate comment from the US, whose delegation walked out of the chamber at the start of Pezeshkian's address.

"The US president described us as terrorists. We have been the victims of terrorism," Iran's president told the UN in New York.

He then held up a photo of the country's late Supreme Leader, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, who was killed in a strike on his residence when the US and Israel launched a joint attack in late February.

He also presented pictures of some of the more than 175 civilians, two thirds of them children, who Iranian authorities say were killed in missile strikes on a primary school in Minab and a sports complex in Lamerd that day. The US has denied striking Lamerd and said it is still investigating what happened in Minab.

"Our innocent people have been the targets of cowardly attacks and aggressions imposed on our country. And we defended ourselves with utmost strength," Pezeshkian said.

Also on Wednesday, an attack on a cargo ship in the Strait of Hormuz killed an Indian sailor, the Agence France-Presse news agency reported, citing Omani and Indian authorities.

The attack was condemned by India's foreign ministry, which called for unimpeded passage through the Strait to be restored.

In February, Iran retaliated for the massive US-Israeli air campaign by launching deadly missile and drone attacks on Israel and neighbouring Gulf Arab states which host US military bases.

It also effectively closed the Strait of Hormuz, through which a fifth of global oil and gas shipments usually pass, by attacking commercial vessels in the Gulf, the Gulf of Oman and the Arabian Sea. The US responded by imposing a blockade of Iranian ports and ships in April.

In June, the US and Iran reached a preliminary agreement to end the war and reopen the strait, but it collapsed within weeks after the Iranian attacks on shipping resumed and the US reinstated its blockade.

Iran wants to retain some measure of control over the strait and collect fees from vessels that use it, which the US has rejected.

In his address to the UN General Assembly on Tuesday, Trump said he faced a "big decision" - either negotiate a deal that would allow Iranians to rebuild their country, or "annihilate the Islamic Republic and do it quickly".

Pezeshkian said the threat was "a sign of a bullying mentality".

"[Trump] must know that the resistance of the Iranian people will only increase in the face of sanctions, increased pressure, increased bullying. We will never bow our head or bend the knee," he said.

But he added: "We are ready for dialogue and diplomacy and negotiations without accepting the language of force."

Pezeshkian made clear that the US blockade would have to end as part of any deal.

"It cannot be the case that everyone benefits from the Strait of Hormuz while we are denied access to shipping through this waterway," he said.

He also reiterated that Iran would not give up its right to have a civilian nuclear programme and that it would not seek to develop nuclear weapons.

"We say it clearly: no nuclear weapons and no limitations on peaceful nuclear technology."

Trump argued in his speech that the war had prevented Iran from obtaining a nuclear bomb and demanded that its leaders "relinquish their nuclear ambitions".

On Tuesday, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi and US envoy Steve Witkoff held indirect talks brokered by Qatari mediators on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York.

Witkoff said he hoped the discussions – the first since June – would "prove constructive and promising", adding that the mediators would continue their work.

But Iran's foreign ministry spokesman Esmail Baqai said the talks were "not anything new" and that Araghchi had maintained Iran's conditions, including the end of the US blockade and the release of frozen Iranian assets.

title: ‘I miss old Google’: readers tell us how they search the internet in the age of AI
description:
A feature called AI Overviews has been a profound change, and the browsing habits of billions of people are shifting
Google has put artificial intelligence at the front and center of its search bar. The most-visited site on the internet still shows the same list of links to users, but they have to scroll past a summarized response from an AI chatbot, a feature Google calls AI Overviews. The change to what was once the gateway to the rest of the internet has been profound, and the browsing habits of billions of people are shifting.
“AI is driving the most significant upgrade of the Google Search experience ever,” wrote Liz Reid, Google’s vice-president of search, last August. In May, the company said more AI is coming.
fullText:
A feature called AI Overviews has been a profound change, and the browsing habits of billions of people are shifting

Google has put artificial intelligence at the front and center of its search bar. The most-visited site on the internet still shows the same list of links to users, but they have to scroll past a summarized response from an AI chatbot, a feature Google calls AI Overviews. The change to what was once the gateway to the rest of the internet has been profound, and the browsing habits of billions of people are shifting.

“AI is driving the most significant upgrade of the Google Search experience ever,” wrote Liz Reid, Google’s vice-president of search, last August. In May, the company said more AI is coming.

As people grow accustomed to AI chatbots, they’re spending more time with Google’s and therefore more time on Google.com. Academic studies are finding that people navigate less to sites beyond Google if an AI Overview can give them a good enough answer, even if the bot cites the sites that feed it. Clicks, also known as traffic, are often the most significant way a website earns money from advertising. Media outlets and website owners are enduring a sustained traffic decline. Large US media companies are suing Google, alleging that AI summaries have redirected and reduced traffic to their sites, cutting into their revenue.

Google said it had not seen a decline in aggregate traffic and that such accusations are based on “flawed methodologies”. Reid, the company’s vice-president of search, wrote last year: “Total organic click volume from Google Search to websites has been relatively stable year-over-year.”

The Guardian asked readers whether Google has improved or worsened in the age of AI and how their habits of searching the internet have changed.

Better, mainly because it leads you in your quest rather than you having to search on yourself. I am happy to have the AI lead me to an answer but the mega caution is that Google AI or any of them are not at all trustworthy. I have had it admit that it was lying to me and apologise! Sionn Achog, retired teacher 76, Dublin

I find that AI responses are more informative than previously, which simply referred the user to other relevant websites. Peter Warb, 75, UK

AI has made Google better. I use AI mode for all my searches. Jose Garcia Jr, 40, recovery coach, Dallas, Texas

AI has improved Google search. The analysis and chat functions are so much more useful than a ranked list of websites that still need to be explored by the user. Reviewing a list of websites is still an option but is very time consuming, and frustrating. Alan Caruana, consultant, 62, Malta

Far more better, faster and real. I search now with confidence, complete assurance and a high degree of accuracy. Eleazar Eke, electrical engineer, 67, Onitsha, Nigeria

Much better. It hasn’t changed my behavior, just getting better and more focused results. Catherine Weber, former political analyst, 57, Oregon

It’s made Google search much better, I find that I rarely actually click on the website links any more. I find information I want much faster and have a deeper understanding of any topic as I can ask questions about it and drill into the areas I’m interested in. Mark Johnson, 52, software engineer, London

Greatly improved it by getting at more arcane info regarding subject matter. Juxtaposition has improved with AI and abstruse knowledge of subjects becomes more accessible to layman. Wonderful tool with power to extend mind through sensing connections and very akin to human thinking. Samuel Lieberstein, 90, retired teacher, Cherry Hill, New Jersey

Search has become worse. Google AI obscures sources and tries to claim information it did not create while diverting traffic from the sources it steals from. Sean Peters, document processor, 41, Portland, Oregon

Every time I search I have to scroll down to find an actual real website to find a full article or discussion or to confirm that the AI summary isn’t making things up. Occasionally when I am feeling particularly bitter, I remember to add the ““-ai”” tag to my search. Ewan Herbert, English teacher, 33, Japan

Worse. I have disabled AI overviews using an extension. Chris Gibson, Dundee

Absolutely worse. I want to be able to decide for myself which results are the most useful and relevant, and we’re no longer able to turn off the AI summary results. Jon Wilkinson, personal trainer, 43, Manchester, UK

Google has been enshittified … I do miss old Google Search and I really hope something of equal capabilities eventually comes to replace it.

The search engine I currently use is good for a lot of things, but if I need to look for something in languages other than English, the quality of the results is much lower. Image search is also not as good as that of Google used to be. Sofia, postdoctoral physics researcher, 30, Lausanne, Switzerland

My first stop now is Duck Duck Go, a pale imitation of Google’s search engine at the height of its powers. Unfortunately, the top results often include Grokipedia entries and other garbage. Craig Garrett, book editor, 52, New York City

I have stopped using Google. I now use another search engine with no AI overviews. Guy Arthur Simpson, writer 66, Spain

I’ve made a conscious effort to find a browser which does not lead with the AI results. Mine is now Ecosia. Dan Jennings, IT, 54, Southampton, UK

I do a lot of research for my studies, and the AI features are a nightmare! I’m still scouring for a decent search engine without any of these ‘AI features’, the last thing i want is to accidentally utilise a water-wasting AI behemoth datacentre when I forget that crucial suffix. I’ve even resorted to using my local library’s resource of legal cases for my work, at least it is trustworthy. Catherine O’Leary, student studying law, politics and sociology, 17, Newcastle Upon Tyne

Google has become almost useless, searches I’ve made in the past which yielded specific results, (news articles, local information, historical references) no longer appear. I no longer submit to Google search first, I go directly to Wikipedia as my first source, then to DuckDuckGo, (with AI disabled) then to Reddit and only to Google as a last resort. Pedro Reyes, 61, Galicia, Spain

title: Have Deletion Anxiety? The Anti-Minimalist’s Guide to Essential Mac Maintenance
description: Whether you’re migrating everything to a new Mac or want to give your machine a boost, this app purges the bloat while keeping your files safe.
fullText:
You’re cruising through a work meeting when your boss asks you to share your screen. Your stomach drops. You have something like 15 tabs open, PDFs scattered from bezel to bezel, and four identically titled Excel spreadsheets to toggle between. Basically, your Mac’s desktop looks like your bedroom did in the eighth grade.

While a messy desktop and digital clutter can be a source of anxiety for many people, it’s actually evidence of your deep work. Between an analyst keeping 15 tabs open so a model doesn't break and a strategist searching through 12 near-identical files right before a Zoom call, the clutter comes with the work.

Running a standard cleanup app to achieve “desktop zero,” or digital minimalism, isn’t always the right solution. It assumes the mess is the problem, and it asks you to interrupt your workflow to fix something that isn’t broken. The fear of accidentally purging a vital draft or dataset is a pain point for anyone with years of research and work stored on their hardware.

An app like CleanMyMac by MacPaw that respects your working files and clears the system junk works the other way around: it's built to go after what's safe to remove, not the files you're actively using. MacPaw, known for user-friendly Mac software like ClearVPN and Eney, built its flagship CleanMyMac app to be a safe, quick way to tidy up your machine.

Your open tabs aren’t the only thing slowing down your Mac; often, it’s the invisible stuff under the hood. Preview a dataset and a cache file writes itself somewhere you’ll never look. Open the same Slack PDF twice and you own two copies of it. Trial an app in March, abandon it in April, and its support files stay behind. None of it shows up on your desktop, but it’s all sitting on your drive.

CleanMyMac tackles hidden hardware weight, OS health, and security threats while keeping you in control of your user assets. The app identifies potential clutter, such as old versions and duplicate downloads, without forcing you into tedious manual folder searches. It then shows you the results so you can review what it found and choose what to remove. The four spreadsheets stay put, because you’re the only one who knows which version is current.

When you open CleanMyMac, the main tool you’ll see is called Smart Care. Click on it, and the software will automatically scan your Mac and purge invisible OS debris.

Here’s a rundown of what the app  does:

Deep cleans: Utilizing Smart Selection technology, it intelligently targets and removes hidden background junk (outdated caches, temporary system files, and broken downloads) while respecting your personal work files.

Scans for threats: Automatically scans for background malware and security threats to keep your online life safe.

Boosts performance: Clears system memory (RAM) and tracks CPU loads to keep your Mac peppy during intense workloads.

Runs updates: Flags outdated apps so you can update them, and when you want to delete them, it clears out hidden leftover files apps leave behind.

Declutters storage: Deletes duplicate files (like those identical PDFs you’ve downloaded multiple times from Slack), similar photos, and forgotten large installer downloads taking up storage space.

Plus, CleanMyMac’s Cloud Cleanup tool will reveal large files hogging up your cloud storage. And the app’s real-time monitors help ensure you always have space available for new files, PDFs, and research materials.

A cluttered desktop, outdated files, and endless email chains aren’t the sign of a scattered brain. They’re evidence of deep, analytical work. What you don't know, and shouldn't have to, is how many gigabytes of cache files and abandoned app leftovers are sitting on your drive.

CleanMyMac by MacPaw clears the background weight, so the only thing competing for your attention is the problem you're actually working on. If you're curious, there's a seven-day free trial to test it out on your own Mac.

title: 10 uBlock Origin Hacks Everyone Should Know
description: Make the most out of uBlock Origin (and uBlock Origin Lite).
fullText:
uBlock Origin is lightweight, effective, and free from shady business practices. Unfortunately, Google's move to Manifest V3 for browser extensions has hobbled ad blockers somewhat. In response, uBlock has split into two products—uBlock Origin and uBlock Origin Lite. The "Lite" version works with most Chromium-based browsers and Safari for iPhone, iPad, and Mac. The full version of uBlock Origin primarily works in Firefox for desktops, laptops, and Android. With those differences highlighted, here are the 10 uBlock Origin (and uBlock Origin Lite) hacks you should know about.

When you use uBlock Origin Lite in Chrome or Safari, it allows you to choose one of three filtering levels: Basic, Optimal, and Complete. The "Basic" filters won't block as many ads as the others, but it also doesn't require access to your tabs and data. These days, most extensions require access to every one of your tabs, which makes uBlock Origin Lite's "Basic" filters an exception that accesses as little of your data as possible.

uBlock Origin and its Lite version both have built-in filters that let you block annoying cookie notices on most websites. To access this in uBlock Origin on any browser, click the extension's icon in the browser's toolbar, and select the gear icon. This will open uBlock Origin's settings page. Under "Filter lists," enable EasyList/uBO - Cookie Notices. This should automatically hide most cookie banners on the internet.

If you see a distracting element on a webpage, you can use uBlock Origin's element zapper to quickly hide it. To use it, click the extension's icon in any browser, and select the lightning icon. You can now click the distracting element, and the extension will immediately hide it from the webpage. In the Firefox version of uBlock Origin, you can also use the picker tool to select an element, and choose from a list of elements to block. For instance, if you want to block a sponsored results widget, the picker tool lets you click the element and choose from different tags associated with the widget. This allows for more precise blocking without having to click the exact spot on the page where the full widget is highlighted.

To use it in Firefox, click the uBlock Origin icon in the toolbar, and select the eyedropper tool. You can select an element, and use the drop-down menu in the blocker pop-up to choose from a list of classes to hide on the page.

In uBlock Origin for Firefox, you have a one-click method to disable JavaScript on any webpage. You can use this to block trackers, annoying features that hijack scrolling, and in general, enhance your privacy. The risk is that blocking JavaScript can also break webpages, which is why you want to try it on individual webpages as opposed to disabling it at the browser level. To try this in uBlock Origin for Firefox, open a webpage and click the extension's toolbar icon. You can then click the > icon to disable JavaScript on the webpage. Reload the page, and Firefox will load it without JavaScript.

In Firefox, you can disable uBlock Origin for a single webpage. This is useful when the ad blocker breaks a webpage or doesn't load some elements correctly. To do this, click the extension's icon in the toolbar, and hold the Ctrl key on the keyboard while clicking the power button icon. Reload the page, and uBlock Origin will be disabled on that specific webpage.

uBlock Origin for Firefox lets you block large media elements on all sites (or single pages). This allows you to reduce data usage on a metered connection. You can use it to block media elements above a custom size threshold like 10KB, 20KB, etc. To try this on a single webpage, click uBlock Origin's toolbar icon, and then click the film reel icon. Reload the page, and you'll notice that certain elements won't load. To set a custom size threshold for these elements, go to uBlock Origin settings in Firefox. Visit the Settings tab, and scroll down to "Default behavior." Enable Block media elements larger than, and use the text box next to it to set the size threshold (in kilobytes).

uBlock Origin and its Lite version have a built-in AI blocker, which includes Google's AI-generated search summaries. To enable this feature, click the uBlock Origin toolbar icon, select the gear icon, and go to Filter lists. You can enable EasyList — AI Widgets. Now, search for anything in Google, and you'll notice that the AI-generated slop no longer appears up top.

uBlock Origin for Firefox has a built-in sync feature that uses your Firefox account to sync settings across devices, but it's not available in uBlock Origin Lite. In Firefox, you can go to uBlock Origin settings, and turn on Enable cloud storage support. Your uBlock Origin settings will then sync to every device where you're logged in with the same Firefox account.

There's also a manual sync feature that works in both versions of uBlock Origin. Head to the extension's settings, navigate to the Settings tab, and select the Back up button. This will back up your uBlock Origin settings to a file and save it to your device. You can use the Restore button on the same settings page to load saved settings to any browser running uBlock Origin. The only restriction is that you can sync uBlock Origin Lite settings with other browsers running the Lite version, while the Firefox version of uBlock Origin can only sync with other instances of Firefox.

Many websites add trackers to links you copy. Sites like Instagram, Facebook, and Threads use sharing links to trace which profile shared the links with you. Luckily, uBlock Origin can block most of these types of trackers. In uBlock Origin settings, go to Filter lists, and enable AdGuard/uBO — URL Tracking Protection. That said, I recommend that you check the URLs before sharing them with others. Sometimes, you may have to manually strip tracking data because no anti-tracking feature is completely foolproof.

uBlock Origin also ships with region-specific blocklists that target trackers from different locations across the world. If you find yourself accessing many websites from foreign countries, you should enable these blockers from uBlock Origin's settings. In the Filter lists tab, click the Regions, languages button to expand the list. This will reveal all country or region-specific blocklists. Enable the ones you need, and you're all set.

title: Why You Probably Won't Have to Verify Your Age With Discord After All
description: Discord's age verification system is now live, but won't apply to more than 90% of users.
fullText:
Discord age verification is officially here. As TechCrunch reports, the company will no longer take you at your word when it comes to how old you are, no matter where you happen to be using the app. Only verified adults can use Discord without restrictions; anyone under the age of 18 will be able to continue chatting on the platform, but with certain limitations.

This change didn't come out of nowhere. Discord originally planned to roll out age verification en masse back in March, but the company quickly pivoted following backlash to its February announcement. That initial news lit the internet up with controversy, as it seemed that Discord was asking all users to upload a government ID to use the service as intended. While the company's plans were a bit more nuanced than that, the criticisms did force Discord to adjust how it planned to approach age verification. Now, those rules are officially here, but the vast majority of users likely won't even notice anything has changed.

The first step, currently rolling out, is to place all users into an "age group." This entire process happens automatically, and requires zero intervention from users—including uploading IDs or other means of authentication. Discord will lconsider a series of identifiers to determine your age group, including how old your account is and what servers you're a part of. The company says it does not look at messages, calls, or content to make these determinations. Based on this initial analysis, you'll be placed into one of three categories:

Adult Age Group: Discord has determined you are 18 or older and can use the platform without limits.

Teen Age Group: Discord has determined you are between 13 and 17 years old. You can continue using Discord with "protections," while adult content and settings are no longer available.

Unconfirmed: Discord cannot determine your age group, and you now have the same limitations as the Teen Age Group. New accounts also fall under this category until Discord's AI gathers enough data to make a determination.

Discord is adamant that the vast majority of users will not have to verify their ages via anything other than this automatic method—the company says more than 90% of users will not be asked to confirm their age, which suggests Discord is quite confident in its models. If you fall into the latter two categories but you are in fact 18 or older, you can still verify your true age with Discord. Following the backlash to Discord's initial plans, you have a number of options for how to verify yourself, including:

App Stores: Depending on your platform, you can let Apple or Google Play share your age range with Discord to verify your age. Your birthday isn't shared.

Google Wallet: Discord can confirm your age using the pass set up in your Google Wallet, which is based on information from your passport.

AgeKey: An independent age verification tool you can use with other services, not just Discord.

Discord also still allows you to verify your age with either an ID scan or a "facial age estimation" (i.e., uploading a video selfie for an AI to determine your age). Discord says that it only receives your age from these data points: If you choose to scan your ID, the other data it contains is immediately deleted, while the selfie video never leaves your device.

If you aren't 18, your account may face some changes due to this new policy. Discord says messages from non-friends now head to your message requests inbox by default, so you must review each manually. Only adult accounts can turn this setting off. Discord will also send you an alert before you accept a friend request from someone you have no mutuals with.

While using Discord, you won't be able to see "sensitive" images; which images are sensitive is decided by the platform's sensitive content filters. You also won't be able to access age-restricted servers or channels, and you won't be able to run commands with age-restricted bots.

While this policy is certainly an improvement over the one presented in Discord's February announcement, it obviously isn't perfect. Discord itself admits that its automated system may get it wrong, meaning that teens may be labeled as adults, or vice versa. Discord may force users 18 years or older to verify their identities when they never needed to before, which will especially sting for users who care deeply about their personal privacy.

But it isn't just privacy-minded individuals who should be concerned. Age verification has been a bit of a disaster for several of the companies that have started rolling it out. Roblox got into hot water after its age verification proved shockingly easy to bypass, letting kids continue to use the platform without limits. Meanwhile, IDscan.net lost over 150 million driver's licenses in a breach this month. Discord doesn't use IDscan.net, and instead relies on Veratad for its ID scan services—but a previous third-party partner, 5CA, was breached last year, exposing ID images.

It's great that Discord has presented some alternative methods of verification, but anyone who chooses to verify via documentation still must send their government ID to a third-party party. Discord says your ID data is deleted once verification is complete, but the whole endeavor requires a lot of trust. All it takes is one weak link in the chain to risk exposing sensitive user records, all in the name of accessing age-restricted features. Yet this appears to be the new norm: More and more states are passing laws requiring age verification for at least some adult content on the web, while countries around the world are beginning to pass social media bans or set limits for minors. It doesn't seem like the unrestricted internet of the past will be around for much longer. Hopefully we don't end up compromising privacy and security in the process of keeping younger users safe.

title: Apple Intelligence Is Taking Up Way More Storage Than Apple Promised on These Devices
description: If you updated to iOS 27 or macOS 27, check your storage.
fullText:
Apple's latest updates are all about AI—Apple Intelligence, that is. When you update to iOS 27 and macOS 27 Golden Gate, Apple will invite you to try Siri AI and other new Apple Intelligence features. (Assuming your iPhone supports Apple's AI features.) But whether you use the new AI-powered Siri all the time or find yourself frequently scrolling past the AI additions, Apple Intelligence is taking up space on your device—perhaps requiring more storage than you bargained for.

I'll admit, I didn't think much of it when I updated my iPhone and Mac to the latest versions. I gave Siri AI a shot, adjusted Liquid Glass, and went back to doing pretty much the same things I was doing before I made the update. But once I saw headlines about how much storage Apple Intelligence actually takes up on these new updates, I had to see for myself. And, wow, were the headlines right: On my iPhone 17 Pro, Apple Intelligence alone takes up 20.65GB. On my M3 MacBook Pro, it takes up a solid 30GB.

These numbers will vary by device: My M1 iMac, for example, only has 13.88GB allocated to Apple Intelligence. But still, these are large slices of my overall storage. Anyone with a small SSD knows how valuable each gigabyte really is, and upwards of 30GB for Apple Intelligence is a lot. Not only that, it's often more space than Apple's own metrics suggest: As MacRumors highlights, Apple says that Apple Intelligence should only take up to 14GB of storage at most, and even less for certain devices. So why is my MacBook Pro allocating more than double that space for Apple's AI?

I can't answer why Apple Intelligence is taking up so much more storage space than Apple says it should. But I can explain why Apple says its AI is supposed to occupy as much as 14GB on certain devices: Apple Intelligence is designed to run on-device whenever possible. While Apple does push certain tasks to its Private Cloud Compute platform, the company wants its AI models to run on your iPhone or Mac whenever possible. This safeguards your privacy, as none of your data has to leave your device to achieve the task—though Apple says Private Cloud Compute also protects your privacy throughout the entire process.

Regardless, for this reason, your iPhone or Mac will download Apple Intelligence models directly onto your device, so it can run processes on-device when it makes sense to do so. If you have a newer or more powerful device that supports Apple's more demanding AI features, like personalized Siri voices, you may need to store more Apple Intelligence data on-device to run those processes—up to 14GB for certain devices—yet it's not clear why Apple Intelligence takes up more than double that storage limit on some devices, like my MacBook Pro.

It's easy to check how much storage Apple Intelligence is taking up on your device, though Apple doesn't make it obvious. To start, head to System Settings > General > Storage (macOS) or Settings > General > iPhone Storage (iOS). Scroll down and choose either "macOS (i)" or "iOS," respectively. Here, you'll see your system storage breakdown, including a figure for "Apple Intelligence."

Unfortunately, there doesn't appear to be a way to tell iOS or macOS to remove some Apple Intelligence models while leaving others intact, or to run all processes through Private Cloud Compute. In fact, it doesn't seem like there is any reliable way to disable Apple Intelligence on a device running iOS 27 or macOS 27 at all. The closest option I can find is to disable Siri (Settings or System Settings > Siri > Turn Off Siri), but while this disables a host of Apple Intelligence options, I still see the models taking up storage on my device, even after a restart. This might be one for Apple to fix in a future software update—hopefully as part of iOS 27.2.

title: Ulster's Hume faces 'number of weeks' on sidelines
description: Ulster centre James Hume is ruled out of Ulster's United Rugby Championship season opener against Edinburgh with a hamstring injury.
fullText:
Ulster head coach Richie Murphy says he expects centre James Hume to be missing for "a number of weeks" after the centre was ruled out of the province's season opener.

Hume suffered a hamstring injury in training this week before Friday's United Rugby Championship opener against Edinburgh at Affidea Stadium (19:45 BST).

His absence will come as a major blow to Murphy, who is already missing midfield options Jude Postlethwaite and Stewart Moore through injury.

Centre David Hawkshaw arrived during the summer.

"James picked up a muscle injury during the week which was an awful pity because he'd put in a huge amount of work and was probably looking the fittest he'd looked in a number of years," Murphy told BBC Sport NI.

"It's disappointing for James and for us as a team.

"But one man goes down, the next man stands up so it'll be an opportunity for someone else."

The Ulster coach added that the 28-year-old could return to action before the conclusion of the series of matches leading up to the break for Ireland's November internationals.

"He'll be out for a number of weeks. It's hard to say at the moment, it's very early in that injury. There's a possibility he'll be back before the end of the block but we're not sure at the moment."

A squad update issued by Ulster Rugby on Wednesday indicated that three other players - Juarno Augustus and summer signings Matthew Devine and Keynan Knox - had participated in team training after overcoming their respective injuries.

title: GB's Reid and Thomas reach finals at Europeans
description: Great Britain's Chantelle Reid and Damar Thomas will fight for gold at the European Boxing Championships after semi-final victories on Wednesday.
fullText:
Great Britain's Chantelle Reid and Damar Thomas will fight for gold at the European Boxing Championships after semi-final victories on Wednesday.

Reid defeated Serbia's Milena Matovic 3-2 in her light-middleweight semi-final, while Thomas triumphed 5-0 over Azerbaijan's Mahammad Abdullayev in the men's super-heavyweight competition.

Team-mates Callum Makin and Dimeji Shittu are also guaranteed medals in the men's middleweight and light-heavyweight divisions respectively after victories in their quarter-finals.

Reid, the Commonwealth Games silver medallist, was behind after the first round against Matovic, but she was the unanimous winner of the second and did enough in the third to seal victory at Asics Arena Sports Hall in Sofia, Bulgaria.

"It was a really good bout. She's a really good girl and I hope we get to share the ring again one day," said Reid.

"On to the next. Each bout's gone better, each opponent's gotten better and I'll be boxing the best out of the weight category in two days' time."

The 28-year-old will face Busenaz Surmeneli in the final on Friday, after the Turkish boxer defeated Russia's Nadezhda Golubeva 3-2.

Thomas, the 21-year-old Commonwealth gold medal winner, will face Russia's David Surov in Friday's final after the Russian also completed a 5-0 victory over Austria's Ahmed Hagag.

Shittu, who had to settle for Commonwealth Games silver in August after a controversial defeat by India's Ankush Panghal, made sure of a European medal with a 5-0 win against Austria's Lucky Aimufua.

The 24-year-old will fight Russia's Cheerav Ashalaev on Thursday for a place in the final.

"My first performance wasn't the best, but that's what I'm like, I go back to the drawing board and showed what I'm really capable of," said Shittu.

"Credit to my opponent. He was game, he was strong, but ultimately skills paid the bills, booked me a place in the semi-finals and a guaranteed medal.

"Last time I brawled, now I want to show that I can box. And the end of the day it's hit or not get hit. So I went out there, put on a show. Got the medal, let's go change that colour."

Makin, a bronze medallist at last year's World Boxing Championships, won 3-2 against Armenia's Marat Mikaelyan.

The 22-year-old will face Azerbaijan's Saidjamshid Jafarov in Thursday's semi-final.

The remainder of Great Britain's fighters experienced defeat on Wednesday, with Lauren Mackie and Amy Broadhurst both losing in the quarter-finals.

Commonwealth Games bronze medallist Mackie lost 5-0 to Lenka Bernadova of the Czech Republic in the women's bantamweight division, while Broadhurst was beaten 4-1 by France's Sthelyne Grosy in the women's lightweight.

Abdul Burton also represents Britain on Thursday, facing Turkey's Semih Gumus in the men's super-bantamweight semi-finals.

He and Shittu compete in the session starting at 11:30 BST, while Makin's bout with Jafarov is among the fights scheduled from 16:00.

title: FA charges Cardiff's Bielik as police end inquiry
description: The Football Association charges Cardiff City defender Krystian Bielik over an altercation involving Portsmouth fans, but a police investigation has been concluded.
fullText:
The Football Association has charged Cardiff City defender Krystian Bielik with misconduct over an altercation involving Portsmouth fans, but a police investigation has been concluded and they will take no further action over the incident.

The flashpoint came during Cardiff's 2-0 Championship defeat at Portsmouth on Saturday, 5 September.

The FA stated: "It's alleged that the player [Bielik] acted in an improper manner around the 71st minute of the match."

The Poland international has been given until Friday, 25 September to respond to the FA charge.

Hampshire Police were notified of the incident during the match and launched an investigation immediately afterwards, but this has been concluded.

A police statement read: "Following an incident involving a Portsmouth FC supporter and a Cardiff player at Fratton Park on 5 September 2026, we have now concluded our investigation.

"After speaking with the complainant and reviewing all available evidence, the matter has been resolved by way of an out-of-court disposal, agreed by all parties involved. As part of this resolution, an apology has been provided by the player.

"The matter is now considered closed, and no further action will be taken in relation to this incident."

Cardiff City have been asked to comment.

Latest Portsmouth news, analysis and fan views

Bielik was involved in a physical altercation with a fan as the 28-year-old went to retrieve a ball from the crowd late in the second half.

Several Portsmouth supporters made gestures that indicated they believed the fan had been grabbed by the throat.

Cardiff head coach Brian Barry-Murphy claimed afterwards that Bielik "got slapped in the face", while clips circulating on social media appeared to show the Poland international grabbing a young fan around his upper body.

In the aftermath, another fan threw a ball at the head of Cardiff defender Perry Ng. Both supporters were ejected from the stadium.

After the game, Portsmouth head coach John Mousinho apologised to Cardiff City's players.

In the days that followed and having been shown the footage, Mousinho said he was "absolutely furious" at the position he says he was put in over the incident.

title: GB sniff Road Worlds chance with Pogacar absent
description: British riders stand a strong chance of glory at cycling's Road World Championships this weekend, with young talent beginning to blossom at elite level.
fullText:
Great Britain's impressive rider line-up for cycling's Road World Championships means the team have rarely stood a better chance of glory.

For the men, there is also the helpful factor of Slovenian superstar Tadej Pogacar being absent, after he suffered crash injuries during the Vuelta a Espana in August.

But at the same time a new generation of British cycling talent is rising, and GB riders could take the coveted winner's rainbow jersey in the men's and women's road races in Montreal this weekend.

While Pogacar crashed out of the Vuelta, the race showcased the continued emergence of 21-year-old British rider Matthew Brennan, who won five stages of the three-week endurance test for Visma Lease a Bike - a record for a Grand Tour debutant.

There are currently 49 British riders competing across the men's and women's world tours - more than ever before - and some of those will compete in this World Championship weekend.

The road race itself is much like a stage of the Tour de France, but in which riders compete in national squads, looking to out-think and out-muscle each other.

A lot of the British potential is thanks to the inspiration of British cycling's golden period, which featured great success from the likes of Team Sky, Mark Cavendish and Lizzie Deignan across the past 15 years.

Deignan won the road race in 2015, while Cavendish triumphed in 2011.

In total, British riders have won the elite road races seven times, including Tom Simpson (1965), Beryl Burton (1960 & 1967), Mandy Jones (1982) and Nicole Cooke (2008).

Amid an unpredictable performance landscape for the women, Britain's best young female riders have a chance to infiltrate the once-dominant Dutch contingent.

Tour de France Femmes winner Demi Vollering remains the sport's best overall, but Briton Zoe Backstedt's brilliant second place in Sunday's Worlds time trial was her first shot at the elite level.

She will be involved in Saturday's women's road race, and Olympic mountain bike gold medallist and Tour de France stage winner Tom Pidcock will race for the men on Sunday.

"You need a lot of faith in your team to be present at the front," Backstedt told BBC Sport. "You need to talk, hear, see and feel each other to know they are there, especially as there's no team radio.

"Obviously it's about knowing the big names to follow. If Demi or Kasia [Niewiadoma] go off the front, you know it's a dangerous move and you need to be there.

"But we've got a super strong team, and if any one of us was with them, we all could stand have a chance."

The women's road race is 180.4km long, which includes eight laps of Montreal, and the men's 273.2km race incorporates 12 circuits.

More Then the Score: How cyclists escape to victory

One key way to win a road race at the Road Worlds is by breaking away from the peloton with a certain distance of the race left to run.

The risk is that one, or a handful, of cyclists find it much harder to win a race by riding into the wind than a peloton of more than 100 riders all taking turns in what can be known as the 'washing machine effect'.

But, if the legs are good and the wind is with them, riders can break away for glory.

"Sometimes you are surprised when you hit the wall, but other times you can push harder and dig deeper," Norway's Sigrid Haugset told the BBC's More Than the Score podcast.

The Uno-X Mobility rider won stage three of this year's Tour de France Femmes after a huge 113km breakaway in which she beat more decorated rivals, such as Belgium's Lotte Kopecky.

"That's the good day - when you feel unstoppable. But I like it when there is plenty of noise [on the team radio from the car]. If it's too little, you get into your head, you feel a bit alone."

Steve Cummings is sporting director at World Tour team Jayco Alula and a former GB rider and breakaway stage winner on both the 2015 and 2016 Tours de France.

Assessing the thrill of a breakaway win, he told More Than the Score: "It's like an underdog victory, and it kind of warms the heart. You have to go all-in. It becomes unpredictable and things can happen tactically and physically - say if a rider pushes too much on a climb.

"That day [in 2015] I did the climb of my life. I was empty for two days after [the 2016 win] and I was in bed for two days after [a Dauphine stage win]. It takes a lot out of you."

To try to chase down a breakaway, the group of differing teams behind must work together to close the gap by using the energy of several riders in the group.

The advantage in numbers should close the deficit to the breakway, who must ride into the wind for longer.

But peloton politics sometimes prevents riders from working together...

title: The footballer who had a heart transplant - then became a World Cup winner
description: Martyn Jackson never thought he'd play football again when he had a heart transplant in 2024. Less than two years later, he was a World Cup winner with England.
fullText:
When Martyn Jackson walked off the pitch after Ramsbottom United's 2-1 win over Cheadle Town in October 2024, it never crossed his mind that one day he could be a World Cup winner.

In fact, in the days after that match, his goal was just staying alive.

Just a couple of days after the final whistle, Jackson started to feel unwell during the night.

He went into hospital and was diagnosed with myocarditis, an inflammation of the heart usually caused by an infection. Within weeks, he was placed on the super urgent waiting list for a transplant.

His life was saved when a donor heart became available, and on 28 November 2024, he had successful surgery at Wythenshawe Hospital in Greater Manchester.

Fast forward to September 2026, and Jackson scored for England in their 5-1 win over Spain in the final of the Transplant Football World Cup.

His team-mates and opponents were, like him, all recipients of a donor organ.

"Obviously, when you've had a transplant, you don't think you're ever going to play again. That's what I thought anyway," Jackson tells BBC Sport.

"I'll be forever grateful to my donor and the family for what they've given me. They've given me the gift of life and the opportunity to live my life to the fullest."

Football at the Transplant World Cup is not quite the same as the game played at the Fifa World Cup.

Instead, it reflects how delicate each player's body is having been through life-altering surgery.

Matches are seven-a-side and played over 20-minute halves. Contact is "not as aggressive as I was used to", Jackson says.

Having played 11-a-side football in the ninth tier of English football before his surgery, he became a game-changing new addition to the national transplant team when he joined up with the squad in January 2026.

Jackson spent his youth career in the academy at Manchester United, before spells at Blackburn Rovers, Preston North End and Burnley. He eventually stopped pursuing a career as a professional and spent 13 years with clubs across the non-league pyramid.

During his recovery, wife Lucy heard about the opportunity to join an England Transplant FC team on social media.

Daley Cross, manager of the England team, said of Lucy's role: "She was just trying to do her best for him and trying to find a way to motivate him.

"His wife did drop in the conversation that he used to play at Manchester United as a schoolboy. So that got our ears twitched instantly.

"You could tell from him being on the pitch, even though he was so fresh into his journey, that he knew the football game and he would be such an incredible asset to us.

"You can be in a dark place, at the time of diagnosis, through your treatment or even post-transplant. So to have us exist to help and inspire people means that we are getting some incredible footballers.

"And that really is the power of it: to that transplant community or to the world, showing people that when you've had organ failure, your life isn't over. There is a chance for you, and you can go and resume and live your life."

As the recipient of a donor heart, Jackson has to manage his exercise workload more carefully than his team-mates, many of whom have had kidney transplants, the most common transplant in the UK.

His role in the side tends to involve 10-minute bursts, rather than playing for the duration of matches.

Bayern Munich's Alphonso Davies was diagnosed with a mild form of myocarditis in 2022. He was sidelined for nearly five months, undergoing specialist cardiac monitoring, before returning to play.

Jackson started to feel ill two days after Ramsbottom side's win over Cheadle, and his case became so severe that doctors had to fit his heart with a mechanical pump to keep him alive.

"Of course it was extremely scary," he says, "but at that stage, when you are critically ill, there's not really much you can do about it. You have to accept it."

The super urgent waiting list he was placed on is the highest priority of the three tiers of patients waiting for a new heart. Typically, only about four or five people are on the list at any one time in the UK.

Dr Paul Callan, a consultant cardiologist at Wythenshawe Hospital's Heart and Lung Centre, worked with Jackson during his diagnosis and recovery.

"Initially, we used to quote an average wait of seven days on the urgent transplant list," he says. "Now it's up to 14 days. Maybe 10% of patients who are put on the list get too poorly and have to be taken off the list."

That increased waiting time is the result of a reduction in the numbers of organ donors in the UK, with a 9% drop recorded in 2026 compared to the same period last year. There are 8,700 people currently waiting for a donor organ, a figure that NHS Blood and Transplant say is an all-time high.

This Organ Donation Week,, external which runs from 21-28 September, the NHS has launched an urgent response plan to address the decline.

Jackson has yet to meet the family of the donor from which he received his new heart. He says he is considering reaching out to them around the two-year anniversary of his surgery.

For him to make a recovery within that time frame, culminating in playing football in a Transplant World Cup, is "remarkable", according to Dr Callan.

England beat six teams on their way to winning last Friday's final in Frankfurt, scoring 36 goals, but for every player at the tournament there is gratitude that they even have the opportunity to play a football match again.

"It is so important to spread that message, have that conversation about organ donation," says England manager Cross, "because our team only exists for that reason.

"I wouldn't have 16 players to manage if we didn't have organ donation. And England wouldn't have just gone and won a World Cup."

title: Eriksen leaves Wolfsburg by mutual consent
description: Christian Eriksen leaves Wolfsburg by mutual consent, just over three months after collapsing during Denmark's friendly with Ukraine.
fullText:
Christian Eriksen has left Wolfsburg by mutual consent, just over three months after collapsing during Denmark's friendly with Ukraine.

The former Manchester United midfielder's contract with the German second-tier side had been scheduled to run until June 2027.

Eriksen, 34, had previously suffered a cardiac arrest during Denmark's opening European Championship group match against Finland in Copenhagen in 2021.

"At the moment, it is important for me to be close to my family in Denmark. I'm pleased that we were able to find a solution together," Eriksen said.

"My time in Wolfsburg was marked by many highs and lows. I know that the club is now in good hands as it aims to make its way back to the Bundesliga, and I am convinced that a successful future lies ahead."

Eriksen, who has not played since June, joined Wolfsburg as a free agent a year ago after leaving Manchester United and made 34 appearances for the club.

The 151-cap international has previously played for Ajax, Tottenham, Inter Milan and Brentford.

In a statement, Wolfsburg's managing director for sport, Dieter Hecking, said: "It was clear that the decision about his future had to be Christian's.

"We wanted to give him that freedom in this particular situation and have now agreed to his request to terminate the contract.

"Despite his short time here, he has left a lasting impression on his team-mates, our staff and the fans."

title: Essex cricketer Das charged with two counts of rape
description: Essex cricketer Robin Das is charged with two counts of rape and will appear in court in October.
fullText:
Essex cricketer Robin Das has been charged with two counts of rape.

The 24-year-old will appear at Inner London Crown Court on Friday, 9 October after he was charged on 23 July.

Das was arrested on 27 August last year following reports of a woman being raped in Brixton in March 2024.

The Metropolitan Police said in a statement: "Robin Das of Queens Road, Waltham Forest, was charged on 23 July 2026 with two counts of rape.

"The charges follow his arrest on 27 August 2025 following reports of a woman being raped in Brixton on 30 March 2024. The woman continues to be supported by specialist officers."

Das, a top-order batter, has made 60 appearances for Essex and last appeared for the club in a One-Day Cup match against Middlesex on 21 July, his only senior appearance in the 2026 season.

Essex have confirmed that he has been suspended since his arrest, two days after his last appearance for the club.

Essex said in a statement: "Essex County Cricket Club can confirm that a male member of the playing staff, currently under contract with the club, recently appeared in court in relation to an incident that took place outside club activities.

"Throughout, the club has remained in contact with the ECB, PCA, the Cricket Regulator and the player with regard to the matter, which included an immediate and ongoing suspension. The club will continue to follow all appropriate legal processes and guidance.

"As a club we have strict safeguarding and HR procedures in place, and all employees of Essex County Cricket Club are required to meet the highest standards of professional conduct at all times.

"As legal proceedings are in progress, the club are unable to make any further comment at this time."

Das made his debut for Essex in 2020 and has made nine first-class appearances for the county, along with playing 29 games in 50-over cricket and 24 matches in T20s during his career. Two of the T20 appearances were for Dhaka Dominators in the Bangladesh Premier League.

title: Ronaldo spurred on by 1,000 goals and Portugal glory
description: Cristiano Ronaldo contemplated retirement after the World Cup but wants to reach 1,000 career goals and help a new-look Portugal thrive before hanging up his boots.
fullText:
Cristiano Ronaldo considered retiring after the World Cup but says he opted to extend his glittering career as he believes he can help Portugal to further success - and reach a personal milestone of 1,000 career goals.

The 41-year-old confirmed in the summer that the 2026 World Cup would be his last, although his long-term future remained uncertain.

However, he has been included in Jorge Jesus' 25-man squad for Portugal's Nations League campaign, which begins against Wales in Lisbon on Thursday night.

In the lead-up to the contest with Craig Bellamy's side, the Al-Nassr forward also targeted the 21 goals needed to reach that magical 1,000 mark.

Asked if he thought about retiring from international duty after the World Cup, Ronaldo responded: "Yes, I did.

"Of course, I'm always thinking on my decisions, my future, the present also. I'm a thinker, you have to think."

The former Sporting, Manchester United, Real Madrid and Juventus player said: "I had a conversation with our president, with our coach. I still believe that I'm able to help the national team to reach what they want.

"I think I can give to the national team my support, not only through the goals, but also outside of football."

Ronaldo is a two-time Nations League winner with Portugal, and he said adding a third title was also an aim alongside his personal ambitions.

"Both aims are important," he said.

"One thousand goals, yes, and the national team. Winning the Nations League, the competition starts tomorrow [Thursday], it's a new age."

Thursday, 24 September, 19:45 BST

Live on BBC iPlayer, BBC One Wales, BBC Sounds, BBC Radio Wales, Radio Cymru and 5 Live, BBC Sport website and app, plus live text commentary.

Young talents including Fabio Silva, Renato Veiga, Nuno Mendes, Joao Neves and Francisco Conceicao all feature in Portugal's squad for this international window.

Ronaldo - who joked he will play on for another decade - says helping his country's newest talents was also a pivotal factor in his decision to continue to represent Portugal.

"This is a new young generation. But for me the basic point is to be on the pitch to score the goals and to help the team win games," he said.

"For me, the most important thing, I know what I am. I know what I do to be here, to have the success that I have.

"I know why young kids love Cristiano, because they see me as an example, and I will continue to do that. Even when I am retired... in 10 years!

"I'm happy with myself. It doesn't matter if I play tomorrow, if I rest the next game. For me, the most important thing is that I feel good."

James had options - but Wrexham not among them

Speaking at a news conference in Lisbon, Portugal boss Jesus described Ronaldo as a "symbol of Portugal and the national team".

It came after the five-time Ballon d'Or winner addressed the criticism he has faced throughout his career - particularly during his time with some of the great clubs of England, Spain and Italy.

"This [Portugal] is possibly where I have felt most cared," Ronaldo said. "From the fans, I also feel the Portuguese like me.

"I do understand that some TV channels like to criticise me, they've tried to kill me with a shotgun, but I can still move away from it.

"Anyway, I am used to it. For over 20 years I have been doing this, but my memories are with people who love me."

title: Itauma 'humiliated' but may never lose again - Hrgovic
description: Moses Itauma may never lose again if he can get over the "humiliation" of his IBF heavyweight title defeat, says Filip Hrgovic, who stunned the Briton in August.
fullText:
Moses Itauma may never lose again if he can get over the "humiliation" of his IBF heavyweight title defeat, says Filip Hrgovic, who stunned the Briton in August.

The Croatian, 34, stopped Itauma, who had been the strong pre-fight favourite, in the ninth round of their meeting at the O2 Arena.

The early signs suggested Itauma had the measure of his opponent, with Hrgovic touching the canvas in the second round and conceding that he was "outboxed" early on.

Hrgovic took advantage when Itauma tired but stressed the 21-year-old southpaw is so skilful that he could go on to have a hugely succesful career if he learns from his loss.

"He's really good. He's special. Very fast, very talented and he countered whatever I tried with his speed and timing," said Hrgovic.

"I never was in the ring before with such a talented kid, with such a fast guy. You have some fast guys but they're small heavyweights. You can handle them with your power but this kid is fast and big. He's got great IQ and great talent.

"I'm still kind of angry because he outboxed me. In my whole career, in 20 years of boxing, I was never outboxed in any sparring or any fight."

While Hrgovic, who wants to unify the division, praised Itauma's boxing abilities, he suggested doubts remain over his mentality.

"It was big shock for him, big humiliation, so maybe it's end of his career if he's not mentally tough. If he recovers from this loss, mentally, it will be hard for anyone to ever beat him again," Hrgovic added.

"A lot of people after that kind of loss, they never come back. So, it will be a hard journey for him to come back.

"You have to go through a ruthless, hard training camp. You need to go through hell to be mentally ready for this. I think he was physically ready but it's the mental part."
