title: Zohran Mamdani Hosts the World
description: Prajwal...
fullText:
In a meeting with mayors from around the globe, Mamdani argued that the left must fix everyday problems—or the right will find someone to scapegoat for them.

On the afternoon of September 19, New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani stood in front of a wastewater treatment plant at Hunts Point in the Bronx and told a group of visiting international mayors that it offered one of the best views in New York City. This was an illustration of Mamdani’s focus on the day-to-day mechanics of city government—sewage, buses, and potholes—and an argument he has been making throughout this year that the socialist left’s credibility will be rebuilt by proving that government can still make people’s lives easier.

Standing with him were the mayors of Helsinki, Barcelona, and Rome, who were part of the group of mayors and city leaders in New York over the weekend for the Urban 20, or U20, a summit of cities from G20 nations. On the sidelines of the summit, Mamdani hosted several left-wing mayors, taking them on a bus tour of New York City and showing them public housing in Brownsville. Mamdani’s office said his meetings with the mayors focused on finding solutions to housing, climate, and migration issues.

Throughout the weekend, it became clear that Mamdani’s pitch for a government that makes life easier for residents has resonated with his international counterparts. At the U20 summit on September 20, Mamdani argued that the left should reclaim phrases like “quality of life,” “efficiency,” and “waste” from the right. “If you are staring at an example of social disorder or social inefficiency, and the left refuses to explain either why it has happened or how they will fix it, then the right gets to point at someone in the immediate area and say, ‘That’s who did it,’” Mamdani said.

The same day, Mamdani said that the movement that made him mayor of New York extends far beyond the city and aims to address the crises of our times—the affordability crisis and the mass migration of millions of people due to climate change and instability. “Those fleeing war, genocide, flood, famine and instability should not be turned away but should be welcomed.… Each of us holds a shared responsibility to provide all our people with opportunity and to view migration not as an obstacle to a city’s success, but, frankly, as fundamental to that success,” Mamdani said.

Earlier this summer, the FIFA World Cup gave the soccer-fan mayor a chance to showcase his idea of a multicultural city in the face of threats from Washington. Even as FIFA priced ordinary fans out of the games, Mamdani pushed FIFA for cheaper tickets and opened up the city for pickup soccer games through the night. On game days in the New York area, Mamdani uploaded direct-to-camera videos in which he spoke about figures like Sócrates, a Brazilian legend whose club, Corinthians, opposed Brazil’s military dictatorship in the 1980s. In another video, he mentioned Brian Clough, the legendary English manager whose Derby County team stood on the picket lines during the 1972 miners’ strike.

The same political instincts were on display again this week as world leaders descended on New York. Mamdani met with Rome Mayor Roberto Gualtieri to discuss housing policy and with Mexico City Mayor Clara Brugada to hand out flyers to delivery workers informing them of their rights under local labor laws. He exchanged soccer jerseys with Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, who is in a tight reelection fight against Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of former president Jair Bolsonaro. And on September 22, Mamdani visited a public school with Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre to discuss AI’s growing presence in classrooms. It is an area of interest for both leaders as New York followed Norway in restricting generative AI for younger students.

Mamdani’s convening of world leaders coincided with the surprise Berlin election win for Elif Eralp, the daughter of Turkish immigrants, who led Germany’s Left Party, Die Linke, to its strongest-ever result in the city on a platform focusing squarely on cost of living and housing. Outlets have already run headlines crediting the influence of Mamdani’s campaign in Berlin after a delegation of Die Linke met with Mamdani’s advisers in New York recently. It has also emerged that political organizations in Europe have studied the canvassing operation that propelled the New York mayor to his election win.

These exchanges have placed Mamdani at the center of the international left as it tries to fight the economic order that has worsened mass migration and made cities inhospitable. “At a time of division and retreat, our cities are choosing cooperation,” Mamdani said ahead of the U20 event. In his closing remarks on September 20, he added, “Familiarity allows us to communicate effectively and openly. It facilitates the lending of policy, the sharing of lessons learned, the exchange of ideas. A transit win in one city informs a newfound ambition in another. A public health success here becomes a blueprint there. That is what familiarity can do. That is the practice of solidarity in action.”

Between the reemergence of right-wing red-baiting and Donald Trump’s use of the chilling National Security Presidential Memorandum–7 to criminalize left political organizing, we’re seeing McCarthyism reborn before our eyes. 

This assault on democracy cannot be ignored or wished away. Resisting it requires bravery in the face of threats and repression, a steadfast commitment to the truth, and the unwavering belief that we can—and will—overcome this darkness.

We must have an independent media that sets the record straight, unearths corruption and abuses of power, and advances a politics of justice and dignity for all if we’re to win this fight.

That’s why I’m writing to you today. This September, The Nation needs to add 100 monthly donors to sustain our progressive journalism. Your contribution makes the next investigative report, the next truth-speaking column, and the next pathbreaking essay all possible. 

I hope you’ll support our work with a recurring donation today. If you donate $10 or more a month, we’ll send you a brand new “Hands Off the Free Press!” sticker to recognise your commitment to our cause. Please, donate today.

Onward,

Katrina vanden Heuvel
Editor and Publisher, The Nation

Tim Janus Dies at 49
description: Janus was an eating competitor known as Eater X who played with Joey Chestnut on 'The Amazing Race' Season 30.
fullText:
Tim Janus, an eating competition staple known as Eater X, has died at the age of 49 after a battle with cancer. Janus, who competed with Joey Chestnut on The Amazing Race Season 30, rose through the ranks of competitive eating and was at one point the second-best in the world, behind Chestnut. Janus was known for competing with a Viking mask painted onto his face.

Janus died on September 16 due to complications from his illness. His death was confirmed by his publicist to Major League Eating on September 20. The statement says he fought a "long battle with cancer." Janus had recently been accepted into the United States Foreign Service and received an assignment abroad, but his illness interrupted his plans.

Janus had a lifelong love of game shows and was successful on several of them. In addition to The Amazing Race, he was the largest winner in the history of Cash Cab and was also a winning contestant on Who Wants to Be a Millionaire?

John Paul Filo/CBS via Getty Images

Janus was inducted into the Major League Eating Hall of Fame in 2026. At the time, he said, "I tell people that I learned a lot about life by eating hot dogs, and I mean it. If you care about something and work hard at it, it makes you better."

"Tim followed his own passions and dreams without regard for the pressures or expectations of society," Crazy Legs Conti, Janus's former roommate and a former world oyster-eating champion, said in a statement. "He was unique, brilliant, and beloved by his friends. He lived his life on his own terms."

Janus was born in Simsbury, Connecticut, on December 31, 1976. He grew up in Connecticut and attended college at Southern Methodist University, where he studied political science and public policy. In adulthood, he lived in New York City's East Village.

"Janus possessed a highly distinctive view of life and an appetite for the unusual that extended well beyond the competitive eating table," his obituary reads. "He sought out experiences with an almost deliberate disregard for the conventional. Among other adventures, he tracked crocodiles and snakes in the wild in Australia, milked a cow, and appeared as a television weatherman on an evening news broadcast. He was a talented whistler, with an eclectic repertoire ranging from Neil Diamond to the Hartford Whalers fight song, in his opinion the best team song ever."

Janus is survived by his mother, Lucinda Hannon, father Peter Janus, stepmother Nancy Janus, and his sister, Tess McNair. There will be a Celebration of Life for Janus in New York City in October.

title: Deion Sanders Claims He’s ‘Most Loving Man’ Then Fires Multiple Colorado Players to Share ‘Tough Love’
description: Deion Sanders entered the 2026 college football season trying to rebuild Colorado after a 3-9 record in 2025. During the offseason, “Coach Prime” made accountability a major focus as he worked to improve the team. Colorado then opened the season with two straight wins. However, that early progress ended with a 41-7 loss to Northwestern […] The post Deion Sanders Claims He’s ‘Most Loving Man’ Then Fires Multiple Colorado Players to Share ‘Tough Love’ appeared first on Gridiron Heroics.
fullText:
Deion Sanders entered the 2026 college football season trying to rebuild Colorado after a 3-9 record in 2025. During the offseason, "Coach Prime" made accountability a major focus as he worked to improve the team.

Colorado then opened the season with two straight wins. However, that early progress ended with a 41-7 loss to Northwestern in Evanston. After the game, Sanders said the team's problems went beyond its play on the field.

After the game, Sanders said he had removed several unnamed players from the team. The "Coach Prime" coach said the decisions were not based only on the loss. He pointed instead to a "pattern of behavior" that he believed was hurting the team. Colorado later said the roster changes were not final and promised an updated list by the end of the week.

According to Sanders, the decision was not based only on one bad game. He said the program had been dealing with a larger pattern of behavior.

"It's never one thing," Sanders said. "I'm the most loving, giving and forgiving man you can ever meet." He added that his patience ends when a player puts personal interests ahead of the team.

That difference matters because Colorado also struggled on the field against Northwestern. The Buffaloes had four turnovers and nine penalties for 80 yards. However, Sanders said the roster changes were tied to behavior beyond that game.

Sanders also connected his decision to problems from last season, when Colorado finished 3-9. He said those issues were allowed to continue for too long. "A year ago, I didn't put my foot down in it enough," Sanders said. "It lingered a little bit. Then, it imploded."

Sanders now wants to address those problems before they grow again.

Colorado's play against Northwestern made Sanders' concerns easier to understand. The Buffaloes gained 348 yards but turned the ball over four times. They also failed on all three fourth-down attempts, helping Northwestern pull away and score 41 points.

Julian Lewis threw for 168 yards and one touchdown, but he also had two interceptions. Northwestern quarterback Aidan Chiles scored five touchdowns, with three through the air and two on the ground.

Penalties have also been a problem early in the season. Colorado has committed 28 penalties for 247 yards. Sanders said that is frustrating because the team plays with more discipline in practice than it has shown in games.

Another issue came up before the Northwestern game. Defensive back Ben Finneseth criticized Northwestern's temporary stadium in a social media video, then apologized during Sanders' news conference. Sanders accepted the apology, showing that different mistakes can draw different responses.

Colorado now needs to apply its standards consistently. Sanders has made those standards clear, but every player must understand where the line is before another issue develops.

Colorado's bigger concern is how quickly another season could fall apart. The Buffaloes went from 9-4 in 2024 to 3-9 in 2025. They lost their final five games and won only one Big 12 game.

Sanders is now trying to deal with problems earlier. That approach matches his offseason focus on accountability and his call for players to give their best effort each day. A recent Gridiron Heroics story also showed that discipline was a major theme before the latest incident.

Still, removing players does not guarantee that Colorado will avoid another difficult season. The roster changes are not final, and the Buffaloes still have a long season ahead. Sanders believes winning starts with putting the team first, so he does not want problems to grow before addressing them.

Colorado will have its next chance to respond Saturday at Baylor. One result will not answer every question, but it could show whether Sanders' warning leads to better play.

title: Tennessee Titans' JC Latham quietly developing into top-end NFL tackle
description: Despite an 0-2 start for the Tennessee Titans, tackle JC Latham is emerging as a bright spot on the line.
fullText:
The Tennessee Titans are off to a rough 0-2 start after losses to the New York Jets and Philadelphia Eagles, and while there have been some uneven moments, there have also been some bright spots.

Through two games, the offensive line has played better than many expected. Although it hasn't been perfect, and they take the blame for some plays caused more by Cam Ward's impatience than they should, it has been a positive start for a group playing together for the first extended stretch.

One offensive lineman who has stood out is tackle JC Latham, who has quietly had a strong start to the season.

JC Latham's ranks this season among OT

Island Rate: Highest
Island Pass Block Win Rate: 5th Highest pic.twitter.com/AJu8rIXMPI

Latham has truly improved as a pass blocker and is showing signs of the player many expected when the Titans drafted him seventh overall in the 2024 NFL Draft. He still has inconsistencies and penalty issues to address, and his run blocking needs to improve, but there is no doubt he's been the Titans' best offensive tackle so far in 2026.

This uptick in performance, combined with the addition of rookie Fernando Carmona next to him, comes at a great time for both Latham and the Titans. title: Rick Barnes is all Vol this weekend with Texas coming to town
description: Another Tennessee-Texas moment for Rick Barnes
fullText:
Tennessee-Texas is far from a traditional rivalry, but it's certainly interesting on a couple of different levels. You have the never ending 'who is the real UT' question, which will never be agreed upon by the two fanbases. That dilemma is funny too, considering the schools have only ever met three times playing football, each coming more than a half century ago in Cotton Bowls.

And then there's Rick Barnes — the legendary coach that Texas grew stale with after 17 years leading the men's basketball program. Barnes made the NCAA Tournament 16 times during his time in Austin, reaching the Final Four back in 2003. However, Barnes didn't make it past the first weekend during his final seven seasons. Texas pulled the trigger on change, and Tennessee was there to happily give Barnes a new home when they desperately needed stability.

Barnes may have even found a better fit in Knoxville, making three straight Elite Eight appearances over the last three seasons. With his old school coming to town this weekend, Barnes was clear who he'll be cheering on.

"Well, I'm pulling for the Tennessee Volunteers," Rick Barnes said on Tuesday. "I can tell you that. And what I would tell you, someone asked me the other day about it. You know, I spent 17 years in Texas, had wonderful friends there. A bunch of them will come in. I doubt I will see them all.

"Really good friends with (Texas AD) Chris Del Conte. I love the guy. He and I got to be buddies when I was in Texas and he was at TCU. And he has done just an incredible job in Texas. And what Danny White has done here, I look at those two guys as being guys that I think if people would listen to them, we could get some things done because they both see things in a different way."

No surprise Barnes is pulling for the Volunteers on Saturday. He's embraced everything about Tennessee from the jump, building the basketball program back from the ground up. He's survived some bad athletic administrations through the years, and now is reaping the benefits of the department finally being on solid ground.

"Obviously, I like to see us because I love Josh Heupel and the way he's building here," Barnes continued. "I think Texas is No. 1. That's why we play the games, right? But, again, I just have so many fond memories of my time in Texas.

"The last 11 years here have been 11 of the best years of my life. And the people I've met wouldn't trade it for anything."

title: Saints vs. Raiders series history: See who has the historical edge
description: The New Orleans Saints have been competing with the Raiders since 1971, but the two teams have only seen each other 8 times. Who owns the series lead?
fullText:
After playing their first two games on the road, the New Orleans Saints play their home opener when they host the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 3. New Orleans enters with a 1-1 record and fresh off a 24-17 road upset over the Baltimore Ravens. The Raiders are a surprising 2-0, albeit with victories over the awful Miami Dolphins and overrated Los Angeles Chargers. Still, the early season versions of both teams look far better than we've seen in recent years.

Sunday marks the 17th all-time meeting between the Saints and Raiders. It's a series that's encompassed Oakland over two spans, Los Angeles, and since their 2020 relocation to Las Vegas. New Orleans is coming off a 6-11 record under then-new head coach Kellen Moore last season, winning four of their last five contests. The Raiders went 3-14 in 2025, the worst record in the league to earn them the first overall choice in the draft. It was their fourth consecutive losing season, and one that caused a coaching change to a familiar face for New Orleans fans. Here is a look at the brief history between these franchises.

Last matchup (2024): Raiders (25-10)

New Orleans has faced off against the Raiders just two previous times prior to this year's matchup on September 27. One of those was in the Superdome to open the 2016 season, won by the Oakland Raiders by a 35-34 score despite 423 passing yards and 4 touchdowns from quarterback Drew Brees, including a franchise-record 98-yard scoring toss to Brandin Cooks. The other September meeting was in 2020, in the first NFL game played in Las Vegas. That was also won by the Raiders in a 34-24 win, in spite of Brees throwing for 312 yards.

Sunday will mark the fourth time the Saints have met the Raiders since that move to Las Vegas. The Raiders have won two of those meetings, which included the 25-10 win in New Orleans when these teams last faced in 2024. The Saints last beat the Raiders in 2022, taking a 24-0 victory in New Orleans. Prior to their move to Las Vegas, New Orleans had a 6-6-1 record against the Oakland/Los Angeles/Oakland Raiders. The only tie between these franchises took place in their first ever meeting during the 1971 season, a 21-21 split at Tulane Stadium.

Probably the most memorable meeting between the Saints and Raiders took place on a Monday night late in the 1979 campaign. New Orleans raced out to a 35-14 lead midway through the third quarter. However, the Oakland Raiders came storming back behind spectacular performances from future Hall of Famers Ken Stabler and Cliff Branch. By the time the fireworks settled, Oakland had taken a 42-35 win.

After the Raiders finished with an NFL-worst 3-14 record in 2025, the team made another coaching change. New head coach for Las Vegas is Klint Kubiak, who was offensive coordinator for the Saints for one season in 2024 during the last Saints-Raiders meeting. Joining Kubiak in Vegas is Andrew Janocko and Rick Dennison, who were also on the 2024 New Orleans offensive staff. Former Raiders kicker Daniel Carlson, with that team for eight seasons between 2018 and 2025, is in his first year as kicker for the Saints.

title: State of the Penguins: Roster Predictions, Season Changes
description: It just began, and it’s already ending. By Saturday afternoon, the Pittsburgh Penguins will have played their final preseason game, […]
fullText:
It just began, and it's already ending. By Saturday afternoon, the Pittsburgh Penguins will have played their final preseason game, and the final roster decisions will come due.

Penguins winger Nick Robertson, who was also part of Kyle Dubas's roster plans when Dubas helmed the Toronto Maple Leafs, quipped on Day 1, "I played in Toronto. I'm used to a lot of guys in camp."

Truly, the Penguins have pushed the limits in this camp, and only a few of the answers are clearer today than they were before camp began. In the end, many of the decisions will come down to preexisting knowledge and perceptions.

And therein lies the basis for projecting the Penguins roster at the start of the 2025-26 season, as well as the mid-season roster, which could differ significantly.

Undoubtedly, the Penguins have an uphill climb in a division that is markedly improved from the last couple of years, when teams squeaked into the playoffs with late flurries to surpass the magical threshold of 95 points. In 2024-25, it took only 92. However, this season will be different, probably to the detriment of the Penguins.

And the standings will play a role in what moves follow.

As we project the final roster, which will be revealed by Monday, a few players are under heavy consideration. PHN has opined that Owen Pickering and Harrison Brunicke have earned NHL spots, but despite their best efforts, it seems unlikely they will break camp with the team.

Obvious keepers: Sidney Crosby, Rickard Rakell, Evgeni Malkin, Egor Chinakhov, Tommy Novak, Ben Kindel, Bryan Rust, Blake Lizotte, Erik Karlsson, Kris Letang, Declan Carlile, Sam Girard. Arturs Silovs.

Essentially guaranteed: Connor Dewar, Nick Robertson, Andrei Kuzmenko, Trevor van Riemsdyk.

Most likely: Kaedan Korczak. Sergei Murashov.

Likely: Elmer Soderblom, Justin Brazeau.

In the battle (Only two can be kept): Hendrix Lapierre, Filip Hallander, Ilya Solovyov, Harrison Brunicke.

Solovyov is a much better candidate than the young Brunicke for a seventh defenseman role and is the likely winner. Solovyov can play both sides and is easily the most physical defenseman on the roster. He was notable Tuesday night. However, Brunicke could leapfrog Korczak and claim a top-six spot. It seems unlikely the Penguins would waive Korczak after trading Parker Wotherspoon to acquire him, but sooner rather than later, Brunicke deserves a spot.

Hallander has been stout in camp and has outplayed most. If camp holds sway, Hallander will claim a regular spot on the fourth line.

On the outside: Rutger McGroarty, Ville Koivunen, Avery Hayes, Tristan Broz, Owen Pickering. Caleb Jones.

It would seem coach Dan Muse has moved Rust down in the lineup, but to great effect. Rust has been paired with Kindel, and the chemistry looked immediate. However, there is one unresolved issue: Robertson with Crosby.

Thus far, Robertson doesn't seem to be part of the clique with Crosby and Rakell, and in fact has had to go into business for himself. Robertson told PHN that it's a work in progress.

For lineup balance and to chase future success, it seems likely that Muse will stick with it for some time, just as he did last season when he tried in vain to pair Chinakhov with Crosby for a couple of weeks.

Just because things begin with the above does not mean the Penguins should keep the status quo. Among the changes, expect Brunicke to force his way into the lineup, which presents a few challenges. On paper, he and Girard would seem to be a bad match; Girard has flashed an ability to control games and doesn't need to pair with a defenseman who is also offensively gifted.

**Letang is the curious point. In the recent past, the Penguins indeed made him available on the trade market but did not find the market to their liking. For those who remember Letang's dynamic skating, his current game is not the same, and the harsh reality of age is closing in quickly. However, the situation is far more complicated than simply deeming van Riemsdyk, Brunicke, or Korczak better and proceeding accordingly.

Dubas finds himself in a spot with Letang.

**The midseason blue line could undergo several changes. If Korczak isn't more than just average, his spot will be in jeopardy to Brunicke. In fact, the Penguins need to find space for Brunicke. How they do it is less important than actually doing it.

**The elephant in the room this season is Karlsson's future. It hangs in the balance and will greatly affect the team. For Dubas, it would be a horrible blunder to keep Karlsson for a playoff chase, miss the playoffs, and then lose him for nothing in the offseason. Karlsson knows the score, and as he told PHN, he's comfortable with whatever happens.

A Karlsson trade could open a couple of spots on the blue line as coaches reshuffle the deck and look for new pairings.

Should the Penguins trade Karlsson? Yes, unless they get his name on a new contract.

In fact, the Penguins' trades this season should have an exit feel rather than an incoming feel. Dubas hasn't indicated he is itching for a surprise, and the market has surely moved away from his trade budget. The runway is lit for the team to transition to the next phase, gain a top-10 pick that could become a future cornerstone, or use it to acquire an established cornerstone, but the question is whether the Penguins will move past this "weird" spot.

**The abbreviated camp has been a difficult read on the Penguins' prospects. Down deep, this writer believes the prospect pool knew they weren't going to make the team and that immutable fact dulled their edge and urgency, just a bit. McGroarty hasn't stood out, but he's flashed his potential on a few occasions.

McGroarty's best hope of cracking the NHL roster this season, aside from injuries, is if the team needs penalty killers. The roster currently doesn't have enough, unless Kindel is pressed into regular service.

**There is a lot to like about Pickering's recent ascension. He's becoming the player he can be, and in a different situation, he would be on the NHL roster Sept. 30. However, if he continues to show the good mobility at both ends and shutdown ability, he, too, will be/should be in the lineup by midseason.

**Ville Koivunen. This camp has probably been the worst-case scenario for Dubas after delivering an eight-year, $32 million contract. Koivunen has not resembled the high-scoring pest that he is in Wilkes-Barre/Scranton and has remained tentative around the NHL players. No player in recent memory has shown a greater disparity between the player they could be, the player they are at the AHL level, and the player they are at the NHL level.

Thursday, we will project the Penguins' season results and the playoff possibilities.

title: Kevin Stefanski: Tua Tagovailoa "trending in the right direction" to be QB2 on Thursday
description: Michael Penix Jr. may not be the only Falcons quarterback returning to the scene in Week 3.
fullText:
Michael Penix Jr. may not be the only Falcons quarterback returning to the scene in Week 3.

Tua Tagovailoa was upgraded to being a full participant on the team's estimated injury report on Tuesday and head coach Kevin Stefanski told reporters on Wednesday that Tagovailoa may be the backup for Thursday's matchup against the Packers.

"We'll see," Stefanski said in his press conference. "But he's trending in the right direction."

Tagovailoa has been sidelined since suffering an oblique injury during practice before the season opener.

Tagovailoa had been in a position to start before suffering the injury. Stefanski said that Tagovailoa has handled the entire situation well.

"Awesome teammate," Stefanski said. "He's working very, very hard to get himself back healthy and he's doing really well there. But just ultra supportive. Great person to have around the building."

Penix is set to start his first game since tearing his ACL midway through last season.

Atlanta's final injury report of the week will be released later on Wednesday.

title: Dylan Larkin is Back With Detroit Red Wings
description: Dylan Larkin returned to Red Wings practice after missing the start of camp with an upper-body injury, though his lineup status remains unclear.
fullText:
Dylan Larkin was on the ice for his first Detroit Red Wings practice of the preseason Tuesday after missing the opening week while recovering from an upper-body injury.

Helene St. James reported that Larkin did not appear ready to take a spot on a line during the practice, with more information expected after the session. Still, his return to the ice marks a meaningful step after the Red Wings began camp without their veteran center participating.

Interim general manager Shawn Horcoff previously said Larkin's injury occurred during off-ice training and that he would need time before becoming available. Larkin also told reporters last week that he was pushing to get healthy and wanted to return as quickly as possible, according to the Red Wings.

Larkin being back at practice does not necessarily mean he is ready for game action or a preseason lineup. St. James' observation that he did not appear ready to join a line reinforces that Detroit is likely taking a measured approach with its top center.

The 30-year-old's recovery comes as the franchise adjusts to a new front-office structure following Shawn Horcoff's appointment as interim general manager. Detroit also remains focused on competing now, with Horcoff previously stating that another rebuild is "out of the question".

For now, Larkin's presence on the ice is encouraging. His readiness for a full practice workload, preseason action and the regular-season opener remains to be determined.

title: Notre Dame women's basketball adds 3 underclassmen to 2026-27 roster
description: Sophomore Maya Gin and freshmen twins Bella and Mia Veith have been added to the 2026-27 Notre Dame women's basketball roster.
fullText:
Three women who came to Notre Dame as students are now student-athletes: sophomore Maya Gin and freshman twins Bella and Mia Veith have been added to the Irish women's basketball team.

Gin is a 5'9" guard out of Hinsdale Central High School in Clarendon Hills, Illinois, just over 100 miles away from South Bend. The Veith twins are 5'6" guards out of Mount Notre Dame High School in Cincinnati, Ohio.

KK Bransford, who played for the Irish from 2022-26 before transferring to UCLA for the upcoming season, is also a Mount Notre Dame alumna. The Cougars went 27-1 in the Veith's senior season, only losing in an OHSAA state championship game.

More: Isabella Sangha doing it all for Notre Dame women's basketball and volleyball

Seventeen games into the season last year, Mia averaged 15.9 points, three steals, 2.2 assists and 3.1 rebounds per game on 38.9% shooting from 3-point range. At the same time, Bella averaged 10.9 points, 3.7 steals, 3.5 rebounds and 1.8 assists per game.

This bolsters Notre Dame's roster to 13 players, one more than last season's 12. It's tied for the second-most on a Niele Ivey-led squad, behind 15 in 2020-21.

While these three additions may not see the floor much, they will be crucial to establishing depth for the Irish in practice, in early-season non-conference games, and in case of injury.

Kyle Smedley is a sports reporter at the South Bend Tribune. Contact him via email at ksmedley@usatodayco.com or follow him on X @KyleMSmedley.

title: ESPN hands out a 'meh' grade to Orioles for very underwhelming 2026 season
description: This was a very "meh" season for the Orioles in 2026.
fullText:
ESPN hands out a 'meh' grade to Orioles for very underwhelming 2026 season originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

The Baltimore Orioles are not going to make the MLB playoffs in 2026, and for all the hype for this team coming into the season, it's another disappointing outcome.

Ever since their 2023 playoff run that looked like Baltimore was a new top contender in MLB, things have gone downhill. While there are some reasons to be optimistic, this 2026 season for Baltimore was very underwhelming.

ESPN's David Schoenfield handed out grades for every team, and the Orioles' grade for 2026 was an entirely justified "meh" grade of a C-, thanks to the questions surrounding a lot of core players on this team.

"Baltimore Orioles: C-. Meh. I mean, you could say that about the entire AL, but the Orioles were especially 'meh' in 2026," Schoenfield writes.

While the majority of the American League was underwhelming, what the Orioles did in 2026 could be best categorized as incredibly underwhelming.

Outside of Pete Alonso, the main stars on this team underperformed. Gunnar Henderson doesn't look like the superstar he once was, and Jackson Holliday might be young but there are a lot of questions about his game.

At catcher, Adley Rutschman was traded to the Boston Red Sox of all teams. Samuel Basallo is someone worth getting excited about, but the mess all across the roster isn't really something to be excited about.

MORE: How Mets, Dodgers and Guardians all made same brutal trade mistake amid MVP races

The starting rotation has a lot of question marks despite some major offseason investments into the position. The bullpen is a bit of a mess, and there is a lot of work to do for the lineup still.

But this season was not a complete disaster like what the Toronto Blue Jays, Seattle Mariners, and New York Mets had. There is still some reason to have hope in this Orioles team moving forward.

That doesn't mean this season should be described as anything other than "meh," as Schoenfield called it. It was an underwhelming season, and one that didn't really move the needle one way or the other.

title: Max Dowman handed England senior squad verdict as Arsenal star eyes record
description: Arsenal's Max Dowman has been tipped to make his England debut in the near future, but the youngest player in Premier League history has been told he must progress through the U21s before earning a senior call-up
fullText:
Arsenal prodigy Max Dowman has been informed that a direct call-up to the senior England squad is not on the immediate horizon, with the U21s identified as his logical next step.

The 16-year-old, who etched his name in the history books as the Premier League's youngest-ever goalscorer last season, has experienced a meteoric rise and is now generating serious discussion about a senior Three Lions berth. He has been on Thomas Tuchel's radar since before the World Cup, but is set to feature with the U19s on Friday.

U21s manager Lee Carsley could find himself welcoming a number of promoted players following the withdrawal of five squad members, including Declan Rice and Cole Palmer, from the senior England setup, which faces four fixtures over the next 10 days, beginning with Spain on Saturday.

Jude Bellingham and Cristian Romero's World Cup feud flares up in Madrid derby

Liverpool captain Virgil van Dijk reaches Netherlands national team decision

However, Carsley has made his position abundantly clear — Dowman's progression will almost certainly run through the U21s rather than the senior squad, as coaching staff look to safeguard his development through a measured pathway they believe will underpin a lengthy international career.

He said, via The Mirror: "It's important players develop at their own pace. Max is an outstanding talent, the timing and the balance of when he comes to the Under-21s is inevitable.

"He's going to the U21s because of his talent, but we have to make sure we do that at the right time. We have to be patient and make sure that ultimately we want them to play for the senior team for a prolonged period. So we have to make sure that we get the time right with that. We had a similar issue a few years ago with Ethan Nwaneri."

Carsley emphasized: "Thomas and I speak regularly about squad selection and obviously Max is always in the conversation because of his talent."

To listen to the latest episode of 'All Out Soccer' - CLICK HERE

The England U21 manager, who has secured back-to-back European Championships with the Young Lions, pointed to the career trajectory of former teammate Wayne Rooney as an anomaly. Rooney leaped through age categories to earn his senior debut at 17 years and 111 days, though that's widely regarded as an exceptional case rather than the norm.

Dowman still has an opportunity to etch his name in England's record books. He has until March 30 to surpass Theo Walcott's two-decade-old mark as the nation's youngest-ever player at 17 years and 75 days old, which Walcott set when he took the field in 2006.

title: Why starting 3-0 matters for the 49ers
description: History shows that it’s way for the 49ers to fast track themselves to the playoffs
fullText:
Several historical trends favor 2-0 teams that start 3-0. That's what the San Francisco 49ers are striving for this Sunday against the Arizona Cardinals.

A loss for an undefeated team in Week 2 is hardly a death knell, as those teams have still made the playoffs at nearly a 62% clip over the past 10 years.

But a Week 3 win that takes you to 3-0 puts you in the same group, and those teams have made the playoffs 73.3% of the time, according to a 10-year study. Even better, you have a 44.4% shot at the division and a 20% shot at the Super Bowl. That's right, a one-in-five chance.

History is on the 49ers' side if they win. It's a club you want to be a part of. Only 45 teams reached 3-0 in a decade, and three of the last 10 Super Bowl champions were among them.

The Seattle Seahawks also fall under this same category. Seattle takes on the Washington Commanders, who are expected to have Marcus Mariota under center. The Niners and Seahawks are headed for a collision course in a couple of weeks where both teams could enter Week 5 undefeated.

The odds to win the division if you fall to 2-1 only drop roughly 5%. Interestingly enough, 2-1 teams have been more likely to reach the Divisional Round than 3-0 teams (by 4%), but it's drastically different once you get into the final two rounds of the playoffs. Those 3-0 teams have a 31.1% chance of making the conference championship, compared to a 17.3% chance with a 2-1 record.

The 2018 Patriots are the only Super Bowl champions in the previous ten years to start 1-2. But five of the last six have started 2-1, with the 3-0 Rams as the exception in 2021.

What matters for the 49ers is that a Week 3 win, historically, is a fast track to the playoffs.

title: Houston Texans NFL Power Rankings: Week 3
description: Where do the Texans land after their loss to the Cincinnati Bengals?
fullText:
Two weeks into the season, and the Houston Texans are already entering a death spiral on nearly everyone's power rankings. It's been a surprisingly difficult onset to the season for Houston, who now has to metaphorically look in the mirror and ask: How much change will be enough to stop this? How many cracks at solving the offensive line does the Texans front office and coaching staff need until it is clearly better than before?

Last week, with last year's trade acquisition RG Ed Ingram sidelined due to a groin injury (which may cause him to miss next week's game), Houston showcased this year's collection of first-year Texans at the interior o-line: Rookie LG Keylan Rutledge, C Evan Brown, and RG Wyatt Teller. The result of another new offensive line combination was another front-row seat to Texans QB CJ Stroud getting pressured nearly every snap, rolling to his left or right constantly, frantically scanning the field as he looked for somewhere to go with this goofy football that has ordained him with a lifetime of torment. When will this be over? When will all of these changes be enough to grant Houston a reprieve at the offensive line position?

As we keep pining for the line to turn the corner, and as the world keeps waiting for Houston to finally look the part of a Super Bowl contender, they continue to drop down the rankings as pundits lose their patience. Once a top ten team on virtually everyone's boards, Houston has destroyed all of that goodwill in just two weeks, and are now facing the reality of being on the bubble of the playoff teams until they have undeniably improved, like last season. In fact, many power rankings author's thoughts on the Texans down below are eerily similar to their criticisms in September of last year, and we all know how the Texans improved down the stretch during that season. Is it possible that we're in store for another midseason surge? Considering how many players are currently on Houston's Injury report that are expected to return sometime this season, I'd say a midseason win streak is very possible, IF they can halt this rash of injuries that has only grown in intensity since August. Unlike last year, I believe Houston has experienced starters at every position group that can be relied on, so as long as they stay healthy, their floor should be much higher than 2025.

Most dropbacks under pressure this season

C.J. Stroud 41
Jordan Love 34
Bryce Young 34
Tyler Shough 34
Caleb Williams 33 pic.twitter.com/LjfpoAgCEm

But that's just what I think, and I'm often blinded by optimism in these dark moments of the season (worked out for me last year). So, let's come back down to reality and check out where the Houston Texans are ranked entering Week 3 of the 2026 NFL Season:

11. Houston Texans (0-2) (Last Week: 12)

I know the history and likelihood of a team starting 0-2 and reaching the playoffs. For those needing a reminder, just 12.8% of clubs beginning a campaign with that record have made the postseason since 1990. I also think the Texans may have landed the worst draw of any NFL team in the first two weeks. Houston competed with both Buffalo and Cincinnati, and C.J. Stroud looks more like the quarterback we've hoped to see. That said, you can't score six points and expect to win.

Week 2 result: Lost to the Bengals 20-6
Week 2 ranking: 11

One thing we know about the QB1: C.J. Stroud just needs a healthy supporting cast.

Stroud has thrown for 627 passing yards in the first two games, third most in the NFL, but that has led to only two touchdowns. The Texans didn't find the end zone at all in Week 2, as No. 1 option Nico Collins missed the game because of a hamstring injury. Stroud's play style isn't necessarily one that can consistently create explosive results when plays break down. He needs the players around him to be healthy so he can produce in structure

Last week's ranking: No. 8
Last week's result: lost to Bengals, 20–6
This week: at Colts

The Texans remind me a little of the Chargers. It looks bad right now, but it's not irreparably broken. Houston is struggling to find the sweet spot in an offense where the tackles are vulnerable in pass protection and not as effective as they need to be in the run game. This is going to take a masterclass from Nick Caley in dressing up his offense while, at the same time, making it easier to grasp for those running it.

Week 2 Results: Lost vs. Cincinnati 20-6

It's still too early for the Houston Texans to panic. However, an 0-2 start is obviously not ideal, and there are some legitimate reasons for concern.

Houston's defense hasn't looked much like the league-best unit we saw in 2025. Wide receiver depth is still a serious issue, and C.J. Stroud continues to look more like an average starter than a true franchise quarterback. However, it may be wise to give the Texans a few more weeks before writing them off as AFC contenders.

The Buffalo Bills have looked like the best team in the conference through two weeks, and Houston was a dropped interception away from beating them in Week 1. Star wideout Nico Collins missed Week 2 with a hamstring injury, and his absence changed the complexion of the offense dramatically.

With three divisional matchups in their next four games, the Texans can quickly climb back into the AFC South race.

24. Texans (0-2) (Last Week: 12)

At 0-2, they are off to a tough start. And both losses are at home. They face an almost must-win at Indianapolis this week.

18. Houston Texans (11): What, we worry? They've now dropped their first two games in three of QB C.J. Stroud's four seasons … and recovered to reach postseason in the first two instances.

19. Houston Texans (0-2, LW: 13)

The Texans' run game was dreadful Sunday when it had to carry the offense with receiver Nico Collins out. The Texans had a putrid 6.7% success rate on runs against the Bengals. Only one team has a mark under 20% in a game this season, and that was the Raiders at 18.5% in Week 2. It's stunning that the Texans have not fixed their offensive line issues over multiple offseasons despite it being an obvious liability.

"For us just collectively as a team, the one key to this victory was controlling the front and from an offensive perspective and we did not control their front," Houston head coach DeMeco Ryans said, via Texans Wire. "We got outplayed up front. We couldn't run the ball well. That forced us into a lot of passing situations."

The Texans bounced back from an 0-3 start to make the playoffs last season, but they're in a big hole after losing two home games to begin this season.

Rookie spotlight: Keylan Rutledge

The Texans took Rutledge in the first round in their seemingly constant attempt to fix the offensive line. It went OK in Week 1, but Rutledge and the rest of the Texans struggled against Dexter Lawrence on Sunday. Overall, things aren't great in Houston, where C.J. Stroud is being pressured on 40.2 percent of his dropbacks, which ranks 24th in the league.

Up next: at Colts, Sunday, 1 p.m. ET

10. Texans (No. 4; 0-2): The offense is letting down the defense.

Average Ranking: 15.89 (Last Week: 10.11)

Yeah…woof. Don't let these rankings discourage you too much, though, because if last year taught us anything, it's that this Texans squad can turn their fortunes around on a dime. Although, backup G Wyatt Teller and RT Trent Brown were supposed to be improvements over former RT/LG Tytus Howard and Gs Laken Tomlinson/Jarrett Patterson, and I have yet to see better results. It's still early in the season, but some of the pressures Stroud had to deal with on Sunday should have been ironed out in the preseason, not during the regular season.

It reminds me of last year, when offensive coordinator Nick Caley and o-line coach Cole Popovich experimented with placing linemen at different positions multiple times until settling on the best lineup roughly halfway through the season. Although, the starting tackles this year (Ersery, Brown) are not expected to be moved around at all this year, so their failures in Sunday's game can be even more worrying since there are no expectations for either player to be replaced by anyone. They're simply going to need to play better next week, and every week after that until the sun explodes.

LOL at the Texans tackles on this play.

Aireontae Ersery (79) and Trent Brown (77) get worked off the line. 

C.J. Stroud stood NO chance. pic.twitter.com/fb3pFYOZ3D

Despite the poor performance from both of them, I'm still cautiously optimistic of Ersery and Brown. They were building blocks to RB Woody Marks' impressive finish to the 2025 season, and they looked okay in Week 1 for the most part! What do you think, though? Will Houston's offensive line finally start moving in a positive direction soon, or are we doomed to watch Stroud suffer behind them for another 15 weeks?

Next week, the Houston Yexans travel to Indianapolis to face the 0-2 Colts in a pivotal division battle for both teams. Houston is trying to get over their ugly loss to the Cincinnati Bengals, and Indy will want to avenge their heartbreaking overtime loss to the Kansas City Chiefs on Sunday Night Football. Both teams have had an oddly similar start to 2026, and each will be desperately clawing at the other to notch their franchises' first win this coming Sunday. Fortunately, the Texans are 5-1 against the Colts in the CJ Stroud era, but how do you think this inaugural 2026 division matchup will go? Let us know your thoughts down in the comments below!

title: Ravens Week 2 film study: RT Roger Rosengarten making Year 3 leap
description: Reviewing the Week 2 film of three of the Ravens’ key starters.
fullText:
The Ravens' Week 2 matchup against the New Orleans Saints may not have produced the home-opening result Baltimore wanted, but there were still several encouraging individual performances in the team's first loss of the season.

Right tackle Roger Rosengarten continued to show signs of a Year 3 leap, displaying the technical refinement and improved play strength that could make him a stabilizing presence along Baltimore's offensive line. Linebacker Trenton Simpson showcased the athleticism and physicality required of a modern NFL linebacker, particularly when playing in space and attacking screen concepts. And with Zay Flowers sidelined, wide receiver Rashod Bateman stepped into the No. 1 receiving role and became Baltimore's primary source of explosive plays through the air. Here's what stood out from that trio in Week 2:

58 snaps | 40 pass blocking | 18 run blocking | 0 pressures allowed | 78.2 true pass set grade

Rosengarten has been excellent to start his 2026 campaign at right tackle with zero pressures allowed through two games and 73 pass-blocking reps.

The biggest development has been his growth as both a technician and a run blocker. Rosengarten's initial strike carries noticeably more strength and conviction than it did earlier in his career. His hand placement has become more deliberate, and he is doing a better job controlling defenders once contact is established. That improvement has carried over into pass protection, where Rosengarten consistently gave Jackson enough time to operate.

There were several reps where Rosengarten either won his pass set outright or, just as importantly, 'lost slowly.' Even when a defender gained an initial advantage, Rosengarten remained attached and forced the rusher to take a longer path to the quarterback, buying Jackson the additional fraction of a second needed to get the ball out.

Roger Rosengarten has allowed 0 pressures on true pass sets this year 

(excludes plays with less than 4 rushers, play action, screens, short dropbacks and time-to-throws under 2 seconds) 

Strong grip strength in the run game to create gap displacement, MMA like pass set usage… pic.twitter.com/rQ7xYp7et5

One particularly interesting addition to his pass-protection toolbox has been the snatch-and-trap technique. Rosengarten used the rusher's forward momentum against him, pulling the defender downward before finishing on top of him. Adding counters like this is an encouraging sign of the technical development taking place entering his third season.

His movement ability was equally noticeable in the running game. On one rep, Rosengarten climbed roughly seven yards beyond the line of scrimmage, located the linebacker at the second level, and sealed him away from the running lane for Derrick Henry. On another, he was able to engage a defensive lineman, flip his hips, and establish positioning to create another lane.

Rosengarten's development could have implications beyond right tackle. If Baltimore can consistently trust him to handle one-on-one assignments without additional protection, the Ravens can allocate chips, slides, and other forms of protection help toward weaker areas of the offensive line.

That makes Rosengarten's Year 3 leap potentially pivotal to the offensive line's ability to improve as a unit. Through two games, the combination of improved play strength, movement ability, and a growing pass-protection toolbox has made him one of Baltimore's most encouraging early-season developments.

42 snaps | 21 run defense | 8 pass rush | 13 coverage | 2 pressures | 5 tackles | 10 yards allowed on 3 receptions

Simpson's performance against New Orleans offered another glimpse at the type of modern NFL linebacker his athletic profile could allow him to become.

What stood out most was his ability to operate in space without sacrificing physicality at the point of attack. On a screen thrown to his side, Simpson worked through a block in space, stayed square to the ball carrier, and secured the tackle for a minimal gain. It was a good example of his athleticism translating into functional pursuit ability rather than simply testing numbers.

His physical development also showed up against the run. On another rep, Simpson met an offensive guard at the point of attack, absorbed the contact, disengaged, and finished the play in the backfield. That ability to take on offensive linemen and work through contact has been an important part of his development.

Trenton Simpson had a impressive week 2 performance

Block deconstruction, attacking in space and dropping to his landmarks to take away passing lanes pic.twitter.com/GjqgdwItpg

Simpson also made his presence felt as a blitzer. On one pressure, he crashed downhill before recognizing the quarterback preparing to throw. Simpson used his high-end athleticism to time his jump and take away the throwing lane, forcing the quarterback to pull the ball down and ultimately contributing to a sack.

The athleticism has always been there with Simpson. The encouraging development is how much more controlled and functional that athleticism looks within the structure of the defense. His ability to process, play through contact, and impact passing concepts in space will be worth tracking as the season progresses.

9 targets | 7 receptions | 88 yards | 1 touchdown | 2.44 yards per route run

With Flowers unavailable, Baltimore needed someone to assume a larger role in the passing game. Bateman answered that challenge with seven receptions for 88 yards and a touchdown while accounting for several of Baltimore's most explosive plays through the air.

One of my criticisms of Bateman in the past has been his ability to consistently get 'friendly' to the quarterback. There have been instances where he could have shortened routes against zone coverage, settled into open grass, and gotten his head around earlier to give Lamar Jackson an easier throwing window.

That wasn't an issue Sunday. On several reps, Bateman recognized the soft spots in New Orleans' zone coverage, adjusted his route accordingly, and presented himself to Jackson. Rather than simply running the route as drawn, he showed a better understanding of how to manipulate space and make himself available to his quarterback.

Rashod Bateman 7 receptions for 88 yards 

Stemming off at the top of his routes, head fakes and selling his cuts. Finding soft spots in zones and sitting down. Got friendly to the qb. pic.twitter.com/xY3f0LDtqc

His route-running ability also showed up against tighter coverage. On two separate plays, Bateman snapped off his route at the breakpoint, combining quick feet with head fakes to manipulate the defender and create separation. Those are the subtle details that have always made Bateman an intriguing route runner when healthy and involved.

The biggest question coming out of this performance is what Bateman's role looks like once Flowers returns. Flowers remains a major part of Baltimore's passing attack, but Bateman showed against New Orleans that he can handle additional volume. Rather than simply functioning as a complementary option, this performance strengthened the case for keeping him consistently involved even when the receiving corps returns to full strength.

Advanced metrics via Pro Football Focus.

title: Green Bay Packers Teammate Doesn’t Hold Back About Jordan Love
description: Jordan Love and the Green Bay Packers were able to avoid a nightmare start to the 2026 NFL season. Following their collapse against the NFC North rival Minnesota Vikings in Week 1, the Packers trailed the New York Jets 17-7 in the fourth quarter of Week 2. Thankfully, the team was able to rally and […] The post Green Bay Packers Teammate Doesn’t Hold Back About Jordan Love appeared first on Gridiron Heroics.
fullText:
Jordan Love and the Green Bay Packers were able to avoid a nightmare start to the 2026 NFL season. Following their collapse against the NFC North rival Minnesota Vikings in Week 1, the Packers trailed the New York Jets 17-7 in the fourth quarter of Week 2.

Thankfully, the team was able to rally and pull out a 20-17 win over the Jets.

Nothing has looked pretty to begin the year. Love has been under constant pressure due to poor offensive line play. Through two games, however, he has been able to throw for 532 yards, four touchdowns, and an interception, although he has completed just 52.1 percent of his pass attempts.

Despite the rough start to the year, Green Bay still has faith that it can be a Super Bowl contender. One of Love's teammates has spoken out before Week 3 action on Thursday night against the Atlanta Falcons with strong words about his quarterback.

As shared by Vince Lovergine of Fox 11 News, tight end Jonnu Smith is clearly a big fan of his new quarterback. Smith was signed to a one-year deal just before the start of the regular season and has been impressed with Love thus far.

"He's a true QB1. Just a great leader," Smith said. "He's got a natural feel for alleviating a lot of pressure in the huddle. He's as talented as a thrower that I've been around."

Over the years since Love took over as the starter from Aaron Rodgers, the expectation has been that a breakout season is coming. So far, Love has failed to have the true MVP-style breakout that fans and the media have wanted to see. He has remained one of the better quarterbacks in the NFL, but he hasn't taken the full leap to "elite" status.

Love has played in 59 games throughout his NFL career. He has completed 63.7 percent of his pass attempts for 12,067 yards, 87 touchdowns, and 32 interceptions. Those numbers show why there is so much belief in Love's ability.

Only time will tell whether or not the 27-year-old quarterback can take that leap this season. The year is off to a rough start, but Love has found a way to continue making plays under pressure. If the Packers can get their offensive line issues figured out, he seems primed for a big season.

Fans will get their next look at Love on Thursday night against a Falcons team that has started the year 0-2. It will also been the home opener for Green Bay at Lambeau Field.

Hopefully, Love and the offense can get back on the right track. Moving to 2-1 would help fans forget more about the Week 1 debacle against the Vikings.

title: What the Team USA players are likely to really think about J.J. Spaun missing out on the Presidents Cup
description: Mark Rolfing believes that the Team USA players who qualified automatically for the Presidents Cup are likely to have had some say in the decision to leave J. J.
fullText:
Mark Rolfing believes that the Team USA players who qualified automatically for the Presidents Cup are likely to have had some say in the decision to leave J.J. Spaun off the team.

Brandt Snedeker's call to overlook Spaun has come under intense scrutiny following his victory at the BMW PGA Championship at Wentworth this past week. Initially, when the 36-year-old was left out, it appeared to be an indication that he was still struggling with the injury that saw him withdraw from the Tour Championship.

However, Spaun was firing on all cylinders on the DP World Tour this past week. With that, there have been plenty of questions regarding whether Snedeker made a mistake by not picking the 2025 US Open champion.

It was exciting to see the likes of Jacob Bridgeman and Jackson Koivun get a chance. Bridgeman proved himself by winning on the same day as Spaun on the PGA Tour.

But Justin Thomas and Patrick Cantlay are divisive figures amongst the fans. Scottie Scheffler had not even made his Presidents Cup debut the last time Cantlay won on the PGA Tour.

Spaun also impressed at last year's Ryder Cup as he won two points from three matches at Bethpage. Nevertheless, perhaps those already on the team were not as keen to see him picked for Medinah.

Speaking on the Golf Channel about the decision, Mark Rolfing suggested that the top six players could have potentially forced Snedeker's hand if they really wanted Spaun on the team.

"I think there's always more pressure on the captain's pick, but keep in mind, even though they're called captain's picks, the other players, the automatic qualifiers play a big part in making these decisions," he said.

"If you think about Scottie Scheffler, the number one player in the world, back in Whistling Straits, he was not on that team, but it was the rest of the team that wanted him on that team, and they all wanted to play with him. He had the support of everybody on that team, and I don't feel quite like J.J. Spaun had that support. I think that's probably what did for him. Ultimately, the responsibility is Snedeker's, but I'm sure the rest of the team that was automatically qualified had a lot to say on it."

Spaun did struggle to back up his 2025 season this year. While he did win the Valero Texas Open, he only managed three more top-10s across the campaign.

And with 10 players needed in each session over the first two days, Brendon de Jonge suggested that Snedeker was justified in not taking a gamble on Spaun's fitness.

"If you look at what J.J. Spaun's done over the last couple of months, he's only got one top-25 and that was in a 50-man field at the BMW Championship. He really didn't have a lot of form. The injury at the Tour Championship, you've got five sessions here, are you willing to take a risk if someone's not 100 per cent? Obviously Brandt Snedeker had to make that decision before J.J. went over and won at Wentworth. Hindsight's also a wonderful thing," he said.

Jim Furyk's decision to pick the top six names available to him for Royal Montreal in 2024 also attracted criticism, particularly with Max Homa and Brian Harman in no form whatsoever.

Harman ended up having a miserable week as he lost all three matches he played. However, with Team USA going on to win comfortably, the debate over Furyk's picks was put to one side.

Team USA should certainly have enough this time around to take the heat off Snedeker.

title: Red Sox’ plan for final week includes stay-ready group in FL, injury returns and iffy weather
description: One takeaway from a long list of Red Sox updates Tuesday? Tanner Houck no longer seems to have a strong chance to make the postseason roster.
fullText:
BOSTON — With the postseason beginning a week from Tuesday, the Red Sox are in get-ready mode. With six games to go against the Guardians and Cubs, the main focus for Boston is getting as healthy as possible while setting up their players for success in the first round of the playoffs.

The next six days will include some important ramp-ups for injured players who are still around the team, a group working out at the Fenway South complex in Fort Myers in an attempt to stay ready and, potentially, a ton of rain that could cause chaos during the final weekend of the year. Here's the latest:

While all eyes were on Garrett Crochet's live batting practice session Tuesday afternoon, he's not the only key Red Sox player who is working his way back. Ceddanne Rafaela remains on the IL with a quad strain he suffered early in the month and both Willson Contreras (hand) and Aroldis Chapman (lat tightness) remain sidelined while active.

While manager Chad Tracy didn't have much to offer on Crochet's next step — "I just know that whatever it is, it's going to be done with Garrett's best interests in mind," Tracy said — he did give encouraging news on the other three, who all worked out before the series opener against Cleveland.

Rafaela, who faced Crochet in the 16-pitch live BP session, is "pretty close" to returning and the Red Sox expect to activate him in the coming days. Contreras is also "doing much better," Tracy said, and swung aggressively both in the batting cage and during an on-field batting practice session.

Chapman, who has not pitched since September 13, is also close to feeling 100% and could get into a game against Cleveland.

"We're a day or two away from him being ready to roll," Tracy said.

One player who remains with the Red Sox but is unlikely to be a factor by next week is Curtis Mead, who is still not at full strength as he recovers from the wrist fracture he suffered on a hit-by-pitch in late July. Mead took swings again Tuesday at Fenway but has not yet faced live pitching and did not get into the box against Crochet. It would take some quick progress for him to be a candidate for the initial postseason roster.

"Haven't ruled it out yet, but's it's gonna be tough," Tracy said. "He's doing overhand BP today. He's been doing a lot of tee and I (said) last week he had introduced a real bat and real ball, tee/flip-type stuff.

"We're getting up against it a bit. We'll see what he's able to do over the course of these next three or four days and figure it out."

Houck, Oviedo among those tasked with 'staying ready' in Florida

In a notable development, the Red Sox did not keep rehabbing right-handers Tanner Houck and Johan Oviedo in Boston after they finished up their rehab stints with Triple-A Worcester at the end of the minor league season last week. Both Houck and Oviedo traveled back to Fort Myers to be part of Boston's "stay-ready" group for the final week.

It doesn't seem, at least at this point, that the Red Sox plan on activating Houck or Oviedo for a spot start this weekend against the Cubs. That would likely put both of them on the outside looking in when it comes to the playoff roster, which is not a total surprise considering the long layoffs experienced by both.

Boston is starting Payton Tolle, Sonny Gray and Ranger Suarez against Cleveland but has not listed any starters for the Cubs series, which starts Friday. On the current roster, Jake Bennett, Patrick Sandoval and Raymond Burgos are candidates to pitch. For now, Houck and Oviedo don't seem to be, though that could change.

BETTING: Sonny Gray 5+ strikeouts against the Guardians is listed at -113 on Polymarket on Wednesday. Also, visit our Red Sox vs. Guardians prediction to view our expert insights.

"You've got to be strategic about that, too," Tracy said. "Keep in mind, you're trying to map out the week now. We've earned the right to get in the position of, final week of the season and we're already clinched. We want to go win games but we also want to make sure we get our bullpen in order and have them very ready to go and fresh for the postseason. A lot of that's going to be based on need, like what do we need now vs. what could we need at the end of the week?"

Complicating matters is that the Red Sox would have to clear roster spots to activate Houck and/or Oviedo and doing so would mean optioning a player to Triple-A Worcester. Any player sent down — like reliever Wyatt Olds, who was demoted Sunday to make room for Tyron Guerrero — would need to stay in the minors for 10 days (unless he's an injury replacement).

Anyone sent down by the Red Sox now would be ineligible for the Wild Card Series roster. It's unlikely they'd want to be in that scenario with lefty Alec Gamboa or righty Greg Weissert, and lefty Jovani Morán is out of options. There might be one spot available if the Red Sox send Burgos down but they likely want to use him for a multi-inning stint to cover innings first.

"It's knowing, whatever you do, if you have to undo that, you put somebody in the window that you can't access (them)," Tracy said. "You've just got to be smart about that."

Houck and Oviedo are joined in Fort Myers by a bunch of Worcester players who will work out there now that the WooSox season is over. For pitchers, Olds, Jedixson Paez and Tyler Samaniego are there. Top infield prospect Franklin Arias is part of the group along with Romy Gonzalez and infielder Tsung-Che Cheng. Interestingly, speedy outfielder Braiden Ward — who remains a candidate to make the playoff roster — is also part of the group and is still in consideration for a spot, according to Tracy.

"All of them could factor in at some point, especially the pitching end," Tracy said. "You just don't know, the next six days, what it brings."

Regarding Ward, Tracy said similar roster considerations about demotions are also in play. Boston already needs to clear one spot (likely by demoting Nate Eaton) to add Rafaela to the roster and needs to have enough capable players to cover the next six games.

Veteran catcher Tomas Nido, who finished the season with the WooSox, is in Boston as an inactive member of the taxi squad.

The Red Sox should be able to complete the Guardians series with no issue but a major rainstorm could wreak havoc with the Cubs in town. That looming threat has, in part, put some roster considerations and pitching plans on hold.

"What I'm hearing is that the weather doesn't look good," Tracy said. "As far as what's going to happen, I don't know. I know there's conversations already going on between front offices and MLB. Everybody is well-aware that the weather could get bad."

Because the Cubs are in a tight wild card race and jockeying for seeding with the Phillies and Padres, it's unlikely the league allows straight cancellations this weekend. Major League Baseball will want all three games to be played, and therefore could move things around with continued showers in the forecast late Saturday into Sunday.

Though nothing has been confirmed, ballpark chatter Tuesday involved a rumor that the Red Sox and Cubs could play a doubleheader Friday and then a Saturday morning game to get ahead of the rain. There are also whispers about a potential move to a neutral site but the Red Sox will try to do everything possible to avoid extra travel before a likely trip to New York.

"I don't know what the ultimate decision there will be," Tracy said. "I just know it's very much on everybody's radar through each organization plus Major League Baseball."

title: Giants' 'biggest problem' includes Rafael Devers, Willy Adames
description: The Giants may not be able to escape this issue.
fullText:
Giants' 'biggest problem' includes Rafael Devers, Willy Adames originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

The San Francisco Giants underwhelmed in 2026.

In fact, they were greatly disappointing.

Does it all fall on the shoulders of first-year manager Tony Vitello? Probably not, and it shouldn't.

"President of baseball operations Buster Posey has voiced his support, so Vitello will likely return for 2027, which puts the pressure on Posey to figure this out," ESPN's David Schoenfield wrote.

As a whole, the organization failed to meet expectations. That includes everyday players who are paid the most on the team.

Large contracts for aging players could make it difficult for the Giants to bounce back in 2027 and in future seasons.

The Giants owe four players over half a billion over the next several years.

"The biggest problem here: Rafael Devers, while rebounding from a terrible start to have a productive season, is signed for seven more years and $223 million; Willy Adames is owed $155.5 million for five years; Matt Chapman, just over $100 million for four years; and Jung Hoo Lee, $65 million for three," Schoenfield added.

"That's a lot of money for a group that combined for less than 10 WAR."

San Francisco should be excited about how Devers finished the season before undergoing core muscle surgery.

He hit .272 with eight home runs, five doubles, and posted a .928 OPS in August. Devers launched seven homers in just 38 at-bats in September.

Still, the Giants owe Devers, and the three other players mentioned, a boatload of money well into their thirties.

In all likelihood, those contracts cannot be easily moved without eating most of the money.

title: Referee for Broncos-Rams game has a history with Sean Payton
description: When the Denver Broncos take on the Los Angeles Rams in Week 3, Sean Payton will be on the same field as a referee he has poor history with.
fullText:
The Denver Broncos have drawn the short straw when it comes to referees in their games this young season, at least if you believe in bad juju when it comes to history.

In Week 1, the Broncos had Clay Martin referee their game against the Kansas City Chiefs. Patrick Mahomes had never lost a game in which Martin was the referee, and that streak continued. Now in Week 3, Bill Vinovich will head the officiating crew in the Broncos' game against the Los Angeles Rams.

Who is Bill Vinovich? He was the referee in a game that featured perhaps the most blatant missed call in NFL history. That was the 2018 NFC Championship Game in which the New Orleans Saints, then coached by Payton, were beaten by, coincidentally, the Rams.

January 20, 2019: Drew Brees pass intended for Tommylee Lewis sails incomplete. Nickell Robey-Coleman on the coverage. No flag. #LARvsNO #NFCChampionship pic.twitter.com/AvzGcpGm2h

Why was no call made? No one seems to know, but it certainly may have cost Payton and the Saints a trip to the Super Bowl. Years later, Vinovich was the referee in the Wild Card round of the playoffs when the Buffalo Bills defeated the Broncos following the 2024 season.

Payton has likely never forgotten that missed call in the 2018 NFC Championship game, and it could possibly be in the back of his head on Sunday night when the Broncos take the field. But just like in Week 1 against the Chiefs, the Broncos can't let a referee be an excuse.

And there could be a silver lining. In their last five games in which Vinovich was the referee, the Broncos have a winning record of 3-2. As for the Rams, in the last five games where Vinovich was their referee, they have a record of 1-4.

At the end of the day, this may not mean much of anything. But if you're superstitious, it could mean a great deal.

The Broncos will face the Rams on Sunday Night Football from Empower Field at Mile High on Sept. 27. Kickoff is set for 6:20 p.m. MT, and the game will be televised nationally on NBC. Mike Tirico and Cris Collinsworth will have the call.
