title: Spotlight on new coaches as road to Afcon 2027 begins
description: Patrick Vieira and Herve Renard are among the high-profile managerial arrivals as the qualification campaign for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations gets under way.
fullText:
Just eight months on from the final of the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations (Afcon) - and with the world still waiting to find out the ultimate destination of the title - the road to the 2027 tournament begins in earnest.

The 48 sides still in contention will play two rounds of qualifying in this extended international window, which gets under way on Thursday.

Two more matches follow in November, with the groups reaching their denouement with the final two fixtures in March.

The top two in nine of the 12 groups will progress to the 24-team finals in Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda.

Preparations for the tournament in East Africa may be lagging behind but, with the three hosts all guaranteed qualification, there is only one spot on offer in their respective groups. That means a second-placed finish may potentially not be enough.

Several managerial changes have occurred since the last Afcon in Morocco and this year's Fifa World Cup, while several star players have hung up their boots. Here's what to keep an eye on in the first two rounds of action.

Senegal appeal date set after Afcon win overturned

Among several coaching changes, two in particular have caught the eye.

Herve Renard, the only man to win Afcon with two different nations, has returned to the Ivory Coast job some 11 years after leading the West Africans to the title.

The 57-year-old Frenchman starts his second stint with the Elephants at home against Ghana on Thursday in what is the standout match in the first round of fixtures.

In the opposing dugout, the experienced Carlos Queiroz is back at the helm after leading the Black Stars to the last 32 at the World Cup. However, Tottenham's Mohammed Kudus is among a number of players to withdraw from his squad.

Patrick Vieira is another high-profile arrival, as the 1998 World Cup champion with France takes charge of Senegal, the country of his birth.

The former Arsenal midfielder, 50, describes the role as "an absolute dream" yet he will begin with two away games against Mozambique and Ethiopia because Dakar is getting ready to host the 2026 Youth Olympics.

Africa prepares for historic Olympic moment at Dakar 2026

Cape Verde were one of the great stories of the 2026 World Cup, pushing Argentina all the way in the last 32 before the debutants lost 3-2 after extra time.

Long-serving coach Bubista has since resigned from the Blue Sharks hotseat, with his former assistant Humberto Bettencourt stepping up.

He will begin his reign in Mali on Friday before hosting Rwanda on Tuesday.

Algeria, Tunisia and South Africa have also changed coaches since the World Cup.

The Tunisians have turned to former Esperance and Renaissance Berkane boss Moin Chaaban as they aim to move on from their disastrous World Cup campaign which saw Sabri Lamouchi dismissed after one game and Renard fail to orchestrate a revival.

Pitso Mosimane has been reappointed by South Africa some 14 years on from his last spell in charge - which saw Bafana Bafana miss out on the 2012 Afcon - and Brahim Hemdani has taken over Algeria after Vladmir Petkovic's departure.

Meanwhile, Afcon legend Claude Le Roy has returned at the age of 78 after signing on for a second stint with Congo-Brazzaville.

The Red Devils have not appeared at the finals since 2015, while Frenchman Le Roy is aiming to coach at a record-extending 10th edition of the finals.

Burkina Faso have turned to ex-Comoros boss Amir Abdou and, after a stint with Libya, 2021 Afcon-winning coach Aliou Cisse has his first competitive matches in charge of Angola.

The former Senegal boss starts with a tough away assignment in Egypt.

Some big-name players have called time on their international careers since the World Cup, with several of them former Afcon winners.

Senegal are looking for a new number one after Edouard Mendy hung up his goalkeeping gloves.

The 34-year-old helped the Teranga Lions become champions at the 2021 and 2025 tournaments - even if the latter title is still disputed at the Court of Arbitration for Sport.

Wing wizard Riyad Mahrez, who captained Algeria to the trophy in 2019, has quit international duty while Ivory Coast will have to cope without midfielders Seko Fofana and Jean-Michael Seri.

Ellyes Skhiri has also called time on his international career and will not be involved as Tunisia aim to reach a record-extending 18th consecutive Afcon.

Meanwhile, Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang has stepped back from Gabon duty, saying he felt "humiliated" by his treatment after their exit at the previous tournament.

The 37-year-old was excluded from the national team set-up after their group-stage exit. That sanction was later lifted, but Aubameyang ruled himself out of Sebastien Migne's Panthers squad despite his fine start to the season with Deportivo La Coruna.

Elsewhere, Eritrea are back in the group stage of Afcon qualifiers - for the first time since the build-up to the 2008 edition - after seeing off Eswatini 4-1 on aggregate in the preliminary round in March.

Chad, Djibouti, Mauritius, Sao Tome and Principe and Seychelles are the other five nations already eliminated.

However, seven Ertirea players absconded after the away leg of their tie which was held in South Africa.

Occurrences of Eritrean sportsmen and women failing to return home to what is a one-party state and a highly militarised society has long been an issue, and was part of the reason for the East Africans withdrawing from qualifying for both the 2023 Afcon and 2026 World Cup.

Yet the Red Sea Camels, who have been drawn alongside Kenya, South Africa and Guinea in Group D, are now largely relying on talent drawn from the diaspora.

Just three home-based players have been named in the squad for their opening two fixtures, which see them take on the tournament co-hosts in Nairobi on Saturday before a 'home' game against Bafana Bafana in Cairo on Tuesday.

Meanwhile, Somalia have reached the group stage of qualifying for the first ever time but face a very tricky draw alongside Ivory Coast, Ghana and The Gambia.

The Ocean Stars are ranked 53rd on the continent but, like Eritrea, can at least dream of reaching Afcon as the tournament returns to East Africa for the first time since 1976.

title: Summer signings assessed & why Town fans can have hope
description: Heading into the international break, Ipswich Town have double the amount of points at this stage of the season compared with their previous Premier League campaign.  Bear in mind as well that they've played four teams who are featuring in Europe this season.  Saturday at Hill Dickinson Stadium - against a team with just their domestic fixtures to worry about - was particularly frustrating, as Gary O'Neil's side didn't deserve to come away with nothing.
fullText:
Heading into the international break, Ipswich Town have double the amount of points at this stage of the season compared with their previous Premier League campaign.

However, I can't help but feel slightly disappointed. While I probably would have taken a tally of six from the opening five matches when the fixtures were announced in June, Town's efforts have, in my opinion, warranted more.

Bear in mind as well that they've played four teams who are featuring in Europe this season.

Saturday at Hill Dickinson Stadium - against a team with just their domestic fixtures to worry about - was particularly frustrating, as Gary O'Neil's side didn't deserve to come away with nothing.

The fact that they did - and will also be without Abdul Fatawu next time because of a daft suspension - leaves a bit of a sour taste.

Let's focus on some of the positives from that afternoon on Merseyside though, beginning in goal, where Christian Walton justified the manager's big call in making a change between the posts.

I was perhaps among the minority in thinking that four games in might be too soon to drop Kjell Scherpen, but Walton looked assured and composed, just as he did when he took a similar chance last season.

He appears to have solved Town's goalkeeping conundrum with little fuss, and deserves to now be given an extended chance in the top-flight. Oh, and there was very little he could have done about Everton's somewhat freak winning goal.

Player of the match Abdoul Ouattara is another that deserves more than a mention.

The 20-year-old, making his first Premier League start, was outstanding at right-back, and justified another big call from the manager in choosing the Ivorian over the more experienced Darnell Furlong, who was so impressive during last season's run to promotion.

Town's plethora of summer arrivals have, in general, given supporters real hope that their latest Premier League stay will be an extended one.

Issa Diop has complemented Jacob Greaves or Dara O'Shea very well at centre-back, while Exequiel Palacios and Sasa Lukic are undoubtedly an upgrade on the midfield starters of two years ago .

That said, they have a long way to go before achieving the club legendary status of Sam Morsy and Massimo Luongo.

In Julio Encisio, Town have a player who can turn a game in an instant, but the surprise package for me has been Emersonn in the number nine role.

I hadn't been expecting a huge amount from the Brazil striker during the early stages of his first spell in English football but, to his credit, he has already become a fixture in the side.

The former Toulouse player has a couple of goals to his name already, and his hold-up play has been very impressive.

With that in mind, it is no surprise that Zian Flemming is still waiting for a first league start in his new club colours, but the Dutchman will be needed further down the line.

He has shown from his cameos so far that he will be ready to take any chance that comes his way.

In summary, O'Neil and his players have given themselves a very good platform from which to kick on, and Town supporters will be relishing the return of domestic football after the internationals, rather than fearing it.

title: Ryan Clark: ESPN chose to "humiliate me"
description: ESPN's latest round of layoffs included the bush-league decision to fire Ryan Clark while he was on the air.
fullText:
ESPN's latest round of layoffs included the bush-league decision to fire Ryan Clark while he was on the air. Apparently, ESPN felt compelled to pull the plug during a break in NFL Live because Outkick was poised to report that Clark would be among those whose time with the four-letter network was ending.

In a recent interview with Craig Melvin's Glass Half Full podcast, Clark addressed ESPN's decision to choose to tell Clark he was being let go during a live show over letting the Outkick report emerge before Clark was informed of his termination.

Ultimately, Clark was happy that it happened in a way that vindicated him.

"If they're patient and they're evil, it never comes to light," Clark told Melvin. "If you're smart enough to say, 'We have these massive layoffs on Tuesday. If we're doing this for the right reasons — if it's about budget, if it's about merging two companies, Ryan gets to find out that he's laid off the day everybody else is.'

"But the evil — right? — the 'want' and will to try to humiliate me, to try to garner favor for doing something you know is foul, backfired, because you give it to mean and evil and hateful people, right? Who you learn a snake gonna do snake shit, right?

"And you may think while you have it in this cage and you feeding it rats, it loves you, but it'll eat you too, right? And so now they see me on TV, they start getting antsy, and because you leaked it to them so they can write a great article about it, they can be so damn happy that Ryan Clark is gone, they're about to out you. That's how it happened. So now these things that were happening to me behind the scenes for an extended period of time, the world got to see it. And because the world got to see it, now I'm not so stupid. Now I'm not so whatever you want to make me. Like these things were really happening."

The threshold problem with ESPN's approach is that one or more people who had the information about who would be laid off couldn't be trusted to keep their mouths shut. While Clark was the only one who was fired while on air, others found out about their fates from media reports and/or reporters before being told by ESPN.

The through line for all of this is that companies either care about their employees or they don't. The best proof as to whether they truly care is if they continue to care once they've decided an employee's services are no longer needed.

ESPN has made its position on that matter obvious. And all current and future employees of ESPN should be taking notes.

title: Chicago Bears sign former Notre Dame long snapper in 2nd stint
description: Former Notre Dame long snapper Scott Daly has been with a handful of teams since he entered the NFL in 2019. He will be joining the Bears once again.
fullText:
Former Notre Dame long snapper Scott Daly is heading back to the Chicago Bears.

According to NBC Sports' Pro Football Talk, the Bears signed Daly off the New Orleans Saints' practice squad and added him to Chicago's active roster.

It is Daly's second stint in Chicago, with the first in 2024 and 2025. The Bears released the former Fighting Irish before the start of the 2025 season as part of final roster cuts.

Daly signed with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in May but was waived in late August. The Green Bay Packers then signed him to the practice squad on Sept. 2 but was released less than two weeks later.

The Saints signed Daly to their practice squad last Friday before he rejoined the Bears.

Daly, an undrafted free agent in 2017, had stops with the Dallas Cowboys (2018) and the Detroit Lions (2021-23). He also played for the San Antonio Commanders of the Alliance of American Football (2019) and the New York Guardians of the XFL (2020).

A Downers Grove, Illinois native, Daly played for Notre Dame from 2012 to 2016. He was the Irish's starting long snapper for three seasons. Daly started in 39-straight games and was perfect on 253 snapping opportunities between his junior and senior seasons.

title: Browns swap out cornerbacks on practice squad
description: Cleveland shakes up their practice squad in the secondary.
fullText:
On Wednesday, the Cleveland Browns announced that they signed CB D'Angelo Ross to their practice squad. In a corresponding move, they released CB Myles Bryant from the practice squad.

Ross was signed by the Browns last November, and played in some regular season games. He competed for a roster spot this camp, but began the season on the practice squad. He was a practice squad elevation in Week 1, before being released September 15. With CB Tyson Campbell banged up, if he has any injury issues this week, it's possible the team will look to elevate Ross again.

title: Astros battling injuries to multiple players, including Jeremy Peña and Cristian Javier, with playoffs on the line
description: The Astros won Tuesday, but lost a handful of players in the process.
fullText:
The Houston Astros pulled off a massive win over the rival Seattle Mariners on Tuesday, but it came at a significant cost. The Astros lost both pitcher Cristian Javier and outfielder Brice Matthews during the team's 7-0 victory.

The injuries come at the worst possible time for the Astros, who moved into first place in the American League West with the win. But with five regular-season games remaining, the team now needs to — at the very least — match the Texas Rangers to actually reach the postseason. Following Tuesday's contests, both teams hold an identical 78-79 record, but the Astros own the tiebreaker.

In addition to those injuries, shortstop Jeremy Peña took a fastball off his forearm late in Tuesday's contest and Daulton Varsho missed the game due to a wrist issue. At this point in the season, any player the team puts on the injured list would also miss the wild-card series, putting the Astros in a difficult spot in the final week of the regular season, per The Athletic.

Despite taking a pitch off the forearm, Peña was initially able to stay in the contest. He scored a run shortly after reaching first base, as Yordan Alvarez hit his 41st home run of the season. When the Astros took the field defensively in the bottom half of the inning, Peña was replaced by Nick Allen. X-rays on Peña injuries came back negative.

Javier and Matthews didn't make it that far. Javier exited the contest after just two innings due to a groin injury. Javier said the injury got worse with each pitch, resulting in him leaving the game. Despite that, he said he still planned to make his last start.

Matthews was removed from the contest in the sixth inning. The outfielder has battled knee issues all season and appeared to aggravate the injury after making a sliding catch in the second inning.

With so much uncertainty surrounding Javier, Matthews and Peña, the Astros either need to play shorthanded in the final week or the regular season or risk losing any of those three players for a possible wild-card series. And the team has to make those decisions knowing every single regular-season game on the schedule is a must-win.

The team can make that decision easier by winning out, ensuring it will make the playoffs. Any stumbles, however, could force the team to make some tough decisions with some of its key regulars.

title: ‘Hard for Me to Buy That’ — Jason Whitlock Bluntly Rejects Michael Irvin’s Bizarre Deshaun Watson-Browns Claim
description: Deshaun Watson entered the 2026 season under intense scrutiny after missing the previous year and facing questions about his place in Cleveland. His difficult Week 1 performance only added to the uncertainty surrounding the quarterback.
fullText:
Deshaun Watson entered the 2026 season under intense scrutiny after missing the previous year and facing questions about his place in Cleveland. His difficult Week 1 performance only added to the uncertainty surrounding the quarterback.

But after Watson responded with a strong showing against Tampa Bay, a debate emerged over whether the Browns even wanted him to succeed. Jason Whitlock pushed back on that idea while discussing Michael Irvin's comments.

Irvin made the claim while appearing on ESPN's "First Take," arguing that Cleveland would have preferred a Watson loss because it could have given the organization a reason to move on from its quarterback.

Watson instead completed 24 of 30 passes for 238 yards and two touchdowns in Cleveland's 23-19 victory over Tampa Bay.

"This is the last thing they wanted. They didn't want him to win this game. They wanted to end this thing right there," Irvin said about Watson.

SET YOUR LINEUPS: PFN's Free Fantasy Start/Sit Optimizer

Irvin's argument centered on Cleveland's decision to evaluate Watson after the team opened the season with two road games. Watson struggled in the 34-10 Week 1 loss to Jacksonville, taking five sacks and throwing an interception, which fueled speculation that Shedeur Sanders could eventually take over.

Watson's response against Tampa Bay changed the immediate picture. He avoided turnovers, threw two touchdown passes, and finished with a 121.9 passer rating. His fourth-quarter touchdown pass to Blake Whiteheart helped Cleveland secure the road win and move to 1-1.

Irvin also pointed to a selfie Watson posted after the victory, interpreting it as a message directed toward the Browns organization. On Fearless with Jason Whitlock, Whitlock rejected that premise by connecting the situation to Browns owner Jimmy Haslam.

BE THE GM OF YOUR FAVORITE TEAM: PFN's Free NFL Mock Draft Simulator

"When you talk about the Browns wanted him to fail, what you're saying is Jimmy Haslam wants him to fail because he's the one that signs all the checks and is spending all the money, and it's hard for me to buy that. There's no one I've ever given $5 to, $50 to, $500 to that I'm hoping that they fail," Whitlock said.

Watson's position remains significant because of the contract Cleveland gave him in 2022. The quarterback signed a fully guaranteed five-year, $230 million deal after the Browns acquired him from Houston.

His time with Cleveland has since been interrupted by suspension and injuries, including a re-ruptured Achilles tendon that kept him out throughout the 2025 season.

Now healthy, Watson has opened 2026 with mixed results across two games and ranks 21st on the PFN's NFL QB Impact Metric. He struggled against Jacksonville before producing a much stronger performance in Tampa Bay, leaving his Week 2 showing as an important development in Cleveland's quarterback situation.

title: Amorim dismissal cost Manchester United £8.2m, but Milan saved them another £8.5m
description: Financial statements confirm Manchester United paid £8.2m to fire Ruben Amorim in January, but Milan saved them another £8.5m by hiring the coach again so quickly.The troubled Premier League club re...
fullText:
Financial statements confirm Manchester United paid £8.2m to fire Ruben Amorim in January, but Milan saved them another £8.5m by hiring the coach again so quickly.

The troubled Premier League club reported a seventh straight annual loss, reaching £43m for the year ending June 2026, increasing from the £33m net loss last summer.

ITALY – SEPTEMBER 16: AC Milan coach Ruben Amorim looks on during the UEFA Europa League 2026/27 League Phase MD1 match between AC Milan and SL Benfica at Stadio San Siro on September 16, 2026 in Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images)

Part of that was down to the decision to fire coach Amorim in January 2026, as he still had 18 months left to run on his contract.

Manchester United confirmed today that their exceptional items for the year included £8.2m severance package for Amorim and his staff, namely Carlos Fernandes, Adelio Candido, Emanuel Ferro and Jorge Vital.

MANCHESTER, ENGLAND – DECEMBER 26: Ruben Amorim, Manager of Manchester United during the Premier League match between Manchester United and Newcastle United at Old Trafford on December 26, 2025 in Manchester, England. (Photo by Carl Recine/Getty Images)

Incredibly, that is less than half what they would've paid out had Milan not snapped the Portuguese tactician up this summer.

If he had not taken on a new job so quickly, then Manchester United would've been footing the bill for £16.7m to cover the rest of the contract.

title: Simone Braglia tips Juventus to win a trophy this season
description: Juventus have shown really good form in their last two matches, providing renewed belief that they can enjoy a successful season. Their recent results have also lifted the mood among their supporters,...
fullText:
Juventus have shown really good form in their last two matches, providing renewed belief that they can enjoy a successful season. Their recent results have also lifted the mood among their supporters, who will be hoping the team can maintain its momentum after the international break.

The Bianconeri had previously dropped points in back-to-back league games, results that brought back some of the negative feelings their fans had experienced during some of the club's worst campaigns. That difficult spell raised questions about whether Juventus could compete consistently across the season.

However, Juve responded positively in their next matches. They thrashed NEC 5-0 in the Europa League before beating Atalanta in Serie A shortly before the international break.

Those results have given the team a stronger platform to build on, and supporters will expect Juventus to continue from where they stopped when domestic and European action resumes.

The Bianconeri now have an opportunity to build on their recent improvement and show that their earlier problems were only a temporary setback. Their performances against NEC and Atalanta have encouraged them ahead of the next stage of the campaign.

When Juventus return to action, their fans will expect the players to maintain the same level of determination. The club will also be looking towards the end of the term with hopes of challenging for trophies.

Juve see themselves as one of the clubs to beat in every competition they enter, and they will continue to fight as hard as possible to achieve their objectives. Winning a trophy would provide a significant reward for their efforts throughout the campaign.

(Photo by Valerio Pennicino/Getty Images)

Former footballer Simone Braglia believes Juventus have the quality and togetherness required to compete for silverware while also securing Champions League qualification. His assessment reflects the progress he believes the team has made in recent matches.

Discussing their season, he said via Tuttojuve:

"Juve can both lift a trophy and qualify for the Champions League. We saw progress in the last match, and there's a unity within the team, even among the current management, that gives us hope."

Juventus will now hope their recent improvement can continue when the season resumes. The team has already shown signs of recovering from its difficult spell, and supporters will be looking for further evidence that they can challenge for trophies before the campaign ends.

title: Colts Alec Pierce to injured reserve; how much time will he miss?
description: The Colts are placing WR Alec Pierce on injured reserve. How much time will he miss?
fullText:
Indianapolis Colts' head coach Shane Steichen announced on Wednesday that wide receiver Alec Pierce is being placed on injured reserve.

Pierce exited the Colts' Week 2 matchup in Kansas City after aggravating his left heel injury—the same one he had surgery on during the offseason.

Rather than undergoing surgery, Pierce is planning to rehab the injury in hopes of returning.

Colts HC Shane Steichen: WR Alec Pierce (heel) being placed on IR. He'll miss at least next 4 games.

"The team and player -- after getting a second opinion -- are hopeful for about a four-to-six-week absence, sources said," Fowler wrote.

Fowler then added, "It's a complicated injury situation, not as clear-cut as some others. How he feels in his rehab week-to-week will be crucial."

Without Pierce on the field for much of Sunday's game, the Colts' offense very much missed his speed. That unit's ability to generate explosive plays without Pierce on the field becomes much more difficult, not only because of his big-play potential being absent, but also because opponents can now defend the Colts' offense more aggressively.

In an effort to add more juice to the passing game, the Colts signed Darius Slayton.

Over the last two seasons, Pierce has led the NFL in yards per catch. He eclipsed 1,000 receiving yards in 2025.

This offseason, Pierce signed a four-year, $114 million deal to return to the Colts in free agency.

title: Video shows police point Taser at Paige Bueckers during Arike Ogunbowale's March arrest
description: Bodycam video captures tense encounter involving Paige Bueckers during teammate's arrest.
fullText:
Body camera footage from the Miami Police Department showed that an officer pointed a Taser at former UConn women's basketball star Paige Bueckers, according to a California Post report.

The footage was recorded during the arrest of Dallas Wings teammate Arike Ogunbowale on the morning of March 5, after players celebrated Ogunbowale and Mist BC winning the 2026 Unrivaled championship.

In the video obtained by the Post, which reportedly took place outside the Miami nightclub E11EVEN, Bueckers had her arms around Ogunbowale and can be heard saying, "We got her." The officer responded by instructing Bueckers to remove her hands from Ogunbowale and raised the Taser toward the former UConn star.

A tense moment involving two Dallas Wings WNBA stars was caught on bodycam. Footage shows an officer pointing a Taser at Paige Bueckers as she attempted to intervene during teammate Arike Ogunbowale's arrest, revealing just how quickly the situation escalated.… pic.twitter.com/bA4cK6HUp8

Ogunbowale was seen being placed into handcuffs on the body camera footage and was arrested around 4:20 a.m., according to Miami-Dade County records cited by ESPN. The four-time WNBA All-Star was charged with misdemeanor battery after authorities alleged she punched a nightclub security guard in the face, but the prosecution withdrew the criminal charge in May before the case went to trial.

From 2015 to 2019, Arike Ogunbowale starred at Notre Dame, earning first-team All-America honors and scoring 107 points in six meetings against UConn. In the 2018 Final Four, Ogunbowale drilled one of the most memorable shots in college basketball history from the right wing to lead the Fighting Irish past UConn in overtime, 91-89, then helped Notre Dame eliminate the Huskies again in the national semifinals the following season during her senior year.

Ogunbowale was selected No. 5 overall in the 2019 WNBA Draft by the Wings and has spent her entire career in Dallas, earning four consecutive All-Star nods from 2021 to 2024. The Wings selected Bueckers first overall in the 2025 draft. Since then, Ogunbowale's scoring average has declined, though she, Bueckers and fellow UConn alum Azzi Fudd have formed one of the league's most productive backcourts while leading a historic turnaround in Dallas.

title: Oklahoma vs. Georgia prediction, odds, pick for SEC clash in Week 4
description: Two contenders in the SEC are set to face off on Saturday in Athens, Georgia as the Oklahoma Sooners visit the Georgia Bulldogs. fullText:
Oklahoma vs. Georgia prediction, odds, pick for SEC clash in Week 4 appeared first on ClutchPoints. 

Two contenders in the SEC are set to face off on Saturday in Athens, Georgia as the Oklahoma Sooners visit the Georgia Bulldogs. It is time to continue the NCAA Football odds series with an Oklahoma-Georgia prediction and pick.

Oklahoma comes into the game at 2-1. After a dominating win over UTEP to open the season, Oklahoma's offense faltered against Michigan. They would not score until the second half, but still were in the game. Jordan Marshall scored in the fourth quarter, giving Michigan the lead, as they won 17-10. The Oklahoma offense struggled again against New Mexico. The Sooners managed just 299 yards of offense while turning the ball over three times. The game would remain tight with New Mexico, despite being a heavy favorite. Oklahoma did go on to win 14-6.

Meanwhile, Georgia has been dominant all season. They opened up with a 63-3 victory over Tennessee State before a 70-20 victory over Western Kentucky. Georgia opened up SEC play against Arkansas in Week 3. The Bulldogs racked up 254 yards on the ground, as Chauncey Bowens scored three times, plus one more from Nate Frazier. Georgia took a 45-17 victory over Arkansas.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Georgia and Oklahoma have met only once. It was the 2018 Rose Bowl following the 2017 season. It was a CFP semifinal, and Georgia beat Oklahoma 54-48.

Oklahoma- DT David Stone (Questionable), LB Kip Lewis (Probable), OL Ryan Fodje (Questionable), OL Jake Maikkula (Questionable), WR Parker Livingstone (Questionable)

Georgia- RB Nate Frazier (Probable), C Drew Bobo (Probable), WR Isiah Canion (Questionable), DB Tyriq Green (Questionable), LB Chase Linton (Questionable), DB Justice Fitzpatrick (Questionable), OL Marcus Harrison (Questionable)

– Oklahoma is 1-2 against the spread this year, but has yet to be the underdog this year.

– The Sooners failed to cover in their only road game of the year

– The under has hit in all three games for Oklahoma this year.

– Georgia is 3-0 against the spread, covering a spread of 24 or more each time.

– The over has been the right side for all three Georgia games so far this year.

The key to this game for Oklahoma is going to start on defense. The defense has been stellar this year, allowing just 7.7 points per game and only 215.3 yards per game. The pass defense has been one of the best in the nation as well, while Oklahoma is 35th in the nation against the run. Oklahoma needs to get Georgia in clear passing situations. Gunner Stockton ran well against Arkansas, running for 97 yards, but also faced pressure. He was sacked three times in the contest. Meanwhile, Oklahoma is the best in the nation at getting pressure on the quarterback, ranking first in sack percentage.

On offense, Oklahoma has struggled to get into a rhythm so far this year. They are averaging just 329.7 yards per game. First, they need to avoid obvious third-down passing situations. The Sooners are converting on just 41 percent of their third-down attempts this year and have struggled to protect John Mateer on third downs. Meanwhile, Mateer needs to use his dual-threat ability. The quarterback has run for just 69 yards so far this year and has not scored on the ground. If the Sooners can unlock the big plays Mateer can make with his leg, it will open up the downfield passing game and possibly jumpstart the offense.

Georgia has been one of the best offensive units in the nation this season. They are scoring 57.5 points per game while amassing 478.5 yards of offense per contest. The offense starts with Gunner Stockton. He has attempted just 45 passes this year, but completed 38 of them for 583 yards and nine touchdowns. Further, Stockton has been protected well and sacked just three times while not throwing an interception. Meanwhile, Nate Frazier has been great out of the backfield. He has run for 202 yards and five touchdowns this year. Frazier was beat up in the Arkansas game but is expected to play.

Meanwhile, the defense needs to continue to be dominant against the run. They are sixth in the nation in opponent yards per rush, and ninth in opponent rushing yards per game. Linebackers Chris Cole, AJ Kruah, and Justin Williams have all shown their ability to get into the backfield on the run. Meanwhile, they are also solid at getting pressure on the quarterback and stopping the quarterback from running. If Georgia can stop the run game for Oklahoma, they will force Oklahoma into obvious passing situations, which could create turnovers.

If Oklahoma is going to have a chance in this game, they are going to need a lot to go their way. First, they are going to need to force some turnovers. With the offense struggling to move the ball, they are going to need short fields to help out. Second, they are going to need to limit possessions for Georgia. Georgia has been explosive on offense this season, and the more chances they get to be on the field, the worse it will be for Oklahoma. They need to sustain long drives, not turn over the ball, and make sure to not come away with empty possessions. That is a lot to ask for a team that has struggled on offense this year. Georgia is a two-touchdown favorite and will cover in this one, on the back of a strong offense.

title: Brian Kelly and Rutgers football? Here's what the former coach is saying
description: Brian Kelly has been connected to Rutgers football should AD Keli Zinn make a coaching change. Here's what he is saying about it.
fullText:
Rutgers football's poor start to the season has drawn speculation and questions about the direction of the program, and that includes whether athletic director Keli Zinn will at some point decide a change of leadership is needed.

One name that has been constantly connected to the job should Zinn ever decide to move away from Greg Schiano is Brian Kelly, who was the head coach at Louisiana State when Zinn and current Rutgers president William Tate were both at LSU.

Kelly, who previously coached at Notre Dame and Cincinnati, is now an analyst with CBS but has made it known he wants to get back into coaching.

He's considered to be one of the leading names in the next coaching cycle.

But being connected to any job right now – while a current head coach is still leading the program – isn't something Kelly is welcoming.

"You can imagine coming from my perspective as a sitting football coach when I was in that position, you hate hearing the rumors because it means somebody's job is being evaluated," Kelly told SiriusXM's College Sports Radio. "I feel uneasy about it. I think we all know it's something that gets out in the media and it's talked about because it's juicy. For me, I just focus on what I'm doing on a day-to-day basis. Those things take care of themselves. Those that are making those decisions, they have a plan."

To be clear, Kelly was not asked specifically about the Rutgers job and he didn't mention the school or Schiano.

While Kelly said he understands it's part of the business, "I don't relish when my name's mentioned for other jobs. I'm pulling for the guy that's got that job and I want to see him do well."

One result of this has also been social media videos and memes circulating about Kelly adapting a New Jersey accent – a reference to the now infamous speech he gave at an LSU basketball game where he seemed to be briefly adapt a southern dialect.

Kelly said his son, who works in operations at Ole Miss, sent him some of the posts.

"I think they just feel like I can fake any accent no matter where I go," Kelly said. "I can do the New Jersey accent. I can do any one you want."

This article originally appeared on Asbury Park Press: Brian Kelly and Rutgers football? Here's what the former coach is saying

title: Former Mexico coach Javier Aguirre takes over Valencia
description: Valencia CF has confirmed the hiring of former Mexico head coach Javier Aguirre.
fullText:
Valencia CF has confirmed the hiring of former Mexico head coach Javier Aguirre.

Aguirre takes over the struggling La Liga side on an initial deal through the end of the season, with the club having an option to extend the contract by one year.

The 67-year-old led Mexico to the round of 16 in a World Cup on home soil over the summer before departing. El Tri legend Rafa Marquez has since taken over as head coach.

COMUNICADO OFICIAL | JAVIER AGUIRRE 

🔗 https://t.co/61kFSP0GXe#BenvingutAguirre#ADNVCF pic.twitter.com/8CNbuUsASR

Valencia sacked Carlos Corberán last week after the club failed to win any of its opening five matches. The historic club currently sits 19th in the 20-team La Liga with just four points from seven matches.

Aguirre brings extensive experience managing in Spain, with previous stints at Osasuna, Atlético Madrid, Real Zaragoza, Espanyol, Leganés and Mallorca.

The veteran coach has also managed Japan and Egypt at the international level.

Aguirre spent two years as Mexico manager, his third stint in charge of El Tri. In addition to the World Cup run, he also led the team to the 2025 Gold Cup title.

title: Fantasy Football: All these struggling offenses have new play-callers — is there any hope for Week 3 and beyond?
description: These teams feature a lot of players we're relying on in fantasy football — here's to hoping they figure things out.
fullText:
I wonder if thriller or action movies have warped our sense of expectation. Take The Karate Kid, Whiplash (underrated), or Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse, for example. Our main character gets put into a situation where they have to learn new skills; the stakes couldn't be higher, and it all culminates in an event where they come out (mostly) on top. However, it's the mastering-of-abilities part that we gloss over.

Training-camp montages and clips of practice don't give us a sense of how much a player is retaining. It leads to the assumption that more time equates to greater absorption. But if the last two weeks have shown us anything, it's that progress isn't linear. Sometimes it takes a moment of clarity for things to click.

And for a few teams, that hasn't happened yet.

A thought just hit me, and I'll share it with you using the gift of hindsight bias.

We've often looked at Justin Herbert as a robot QB. He'll check all his reads, make the risk calculations on the fly and throw the optimal pass. Herbert's been more aggressive as of late, but you'll still catch shades of it depending on the situation.

Anyway, contrast his play-execution approach to OC Mike McDaniel's style. The guy who ponders mortality, but has the sneaker mindset of a 20-year-old. You couldn't find two more dissimilar people outside of their love for football. So, communicating the details might be hard for the Chargers' OC and QB.

the Chargers are a comedy of errors pic.twitter.com/4ApaQL5XKQ

To be clear, and as Josh indicates above, this is a collective failure. I'll get to Herbert's part in all of this in a bit, but even staying at the team level gives us an idea of what's changed.

Pre-Snap Motion: 50.0% (2025), 73.8% (2026)

Play-Action Pass Rate (Early Downs): 32.0%, 42.5%

Remember, heavy motion before the snap with an intermediate or deep shot off a play-action concept was a staple of the Dolphins offense. And we loved it. Well, we liked it, mostly because it worked. Or when it did, we'd get the explosive plays that would show up in the box scores of Tyreek Hill or Jaylen Waddle. But there's a tradeoff.

Pre-snap motion can help receivers get up to their top speed faster. The payoff is throwing the ball farther downfield, and that's what Herbert has done through two weeks. His passing aDOT is up 19.4% to 9.2 air yards. On play-action reads, it's at 10.6!

But more time before the snap plus longer routes downfield takes more time off the clock, leaving the Chargers with fewer plays per game. Or, said another way, they've reduced their number of chances to pick up yards under the assumption an efficiency bump will give them the edge. This all sounds reasonable because we've seen it work before. And that's part of why the finger-pointing goes toward No. 10.

aDOT (using Play Action): 8.0 (2025), 10.6 (2026)

CPOE: +1.57% (2025), -6.24% (2026)

Admittedly, I'm presenting you with Herbert's numbers in bad faith. Sure, if you were asking your QB to throw farther under more pressure, a steep drop in their completion percentage shouldn't be a surprise. Such is the case for the Chargers' QB1. But I'll give you a few more metrics to contextualize the situation.

(Early Down) Pass Rate Over Expectation: +1.91% (2025), -10.5% (2026)

Adj. Yards Before Contact per Att.: 0.68, 0.75

Yardage Needed on Third Downs: 6.7, 8.5

Like any McDaniel system, the play sequencing relies on the combination of the rush and the pass. Accordingly, L.A.'s early-down PROE has dropped as compared to '25. But Omarion Hampton's push from the interior offensive line to get to the LOS hasn't improved. The result is Herbert and co. needing to go an extra two yards for a new set of downs. And even when he's found the right throw, calamity still follows.

yeah hole shots to the field aren't your usual fare but just another play that goes as an incompletion https://t.co/onVtXvzdr0 pic.twitter.com/vLq4qGkQhR

Because there are so few samples, intermediate attempts with at least a yard of separation will act like an anchor to a passer's CPOE. That should be an "easy" completion. But Herbert's receivers already have three drops collectively. Which could be why Herbert started to view the shorter passes as the better option versus letting it fly later in the game.

The losses are the exclamation point on all this. Without the full mastery of the offense, flashes are all we'll get until things click between Herbert and McDaniel. Ladd McConkey is still a WR2 (when healthy), and Hampton ranks ninth in team rush rate. Along with Herbert, they're your only viable starters until the QB-OC mind meld is complete.

So, I wanted to revisit the Buccaneers after my initial takeaways from their inexplicable loss to the Browns. Not to walk anything back, but to give a more forward-looking view. Tampa has three players with a top-100 ADP. Even some stability to the offense would be nice. Let's look for the signs that things are back on track.

Baker Mayfield blocking for Bucky Irving 😤 pic.twitter.com/kfC0tRMcGY

No, I'm not advocating for Baker Mayfield taking on an extra job as a lead blocker. Let's focus on Bucky Irving's big run. Over the past two weeks, Tampa has split its early-down play calls between run and pass (-1.27% PROE). That means Irving's results have as much of an impact as Mayfield's. And we saw that influence on Sunday.

(Early-Down) Rushing Success Rate: 62.5% (at CIN), 37.5% (vs CLE)

Forced Missed Tackle Rate: 62.5%, 12.5%

Third-Down Yardage Needed: 6.0, 9.2

Unfortunately for my argument, I'd expect to see RBs bouncing off Bengals' defenders at a high rate. But an 80% drop isn't just about the opponent. Irving's adjusted yards per contact also fell by more than half. And the cascade effect put Mayfield at nearly 10 yards to go on third down. His Week 3 rival (Vikings) might not allow it, but Weeks 4-9 feature favorable matchups for Irving, making life easier for the passing game. But Mayfield can also help himself.

Baker Mayfield connects with Tez Johnson for a 49 yard completion #WeAreTheKrewe #CLEvsTB pic.twitter.com/2bfac6BCS2

I'll make a simple statement: making big plays is a good thing! But a "peaks and valleys" passing game has a short half-life after a big burst. And it looked like Mayfield understood that against Cincinnati.

Passing aDOT (early downs, play-action): 6.0 (at CIN), 11.3 (vs CLE)

Passing Success Rate: 47.8%, 38.5%

At least on the surface, these are the same problems the Chargers are experiencing. A less efficient running game leads to an overcompensating aerial attack. A third of Mayfield's attempts on early downs using play-action concepts against the Bengals turned into a first down. That same rate fell to 20.0% against the Browns as his aDOT nearly doubled.

Mayfield had four pass-catchers average eight or more yards AFTER the catch per reception in Week 1. From Irving to Chris Godwin Jr., a short-to-intermediate plan not only extended drives, but (mostly) kept Mayfield upright. Ted Hurst and Tez Johnson will always be downfield threats. But finding a rhythm with his interior receivers will keep the offense on schedule and fantasy managers happy.

I started the Eagles defense in the Yahoo Expert league, under the assumption that they'd prey on Cam Ward's mistake-prone nature. But as I kept getting more updates about the game and Philadelphia's narrow loss, I decided to take a walk down Narrative Street regarding Tennessee's sudden reversal of fortune on offense.

Take 1: HC Brian Daboll still knows how to game plan.

Nothing about the Titans' Week 1 offense indicated they could hang with the Eagles. Jayden Daniels' mobility and Stefon Diggs' route-running skills were the Commanders' superpower against them the prior week. Tennessee can't boast the same talent. But there was something about Philadelphia's defense that Daboll could attack.

Does the Titans' new logo stand for Tennessee or Power T? 💭 #TitanUp #RTDB pic.twitter.com/aQE3cVfkvl

Before anyone with a 215 area code starts hollering at me, I recognize this is just one play. But Sunday was Tony Pollard's first outing with a rushing success rate at or above 50.0% against a solid rushing defense since Week 3 of last year. And Tyjae Spears wasn't too far behind his RB1 with 70 all-purpose yards.

The results don't matter to us because the single-digit PPR point totals are insignificant. But Philadelphia closed out the final month of the '25 season as a league-average run defense, returned most of its starters and opened 2026 allowing the seventh-most first downs on the ground to RBs. Fittingly, Week 2 was when Daboll, the former Giants' HC who played against the Eagles twice a year, decided to adjust Tennessee's offensive tendencies.

PROE: +5.4% (Week 1), -20.1% (Week 2)

Under-Center Passing Rate: 8.6%, 27.3%

Again, I'm trying not to focus on the results. Instead, let's look for the signs of an offense prepared for its opponent. And at least for this one matchup, the Titans understood the assignment by pulling on the levers needed to limit the Eagles' possessions while maximizing theirs. They averaged over 25 yards per drive for the first time since playing the Mahomes-less Chiefs. Even better, Ward showed some signs of life as a QB.

Take 2: Cam Ward is buying into how to be an effective passer.

I'll be the first to admit Ward is still leaving plays on the field. But let's compare his passing charts over his last two games.

He's throwing fewer passes to the boundary while allowing his receivers to work after the catch. His CPOE flipping from -5.6% to +3.4% is our first encouraging sign. But so is his YAC per completion nearly doubling from 3.9 to 7.7. And that's not from a single play.

Elic Ayomanor picked up chunk plays on two intermediate targets. Spears (14.0 YAC per reception) and Pollard (8.0) also contributed to giving the offense a fresh set of downs. And even though Carnell Tate only turned in 27 scoreless yards, his shortened aDOT (9.8) and team-leading target share (29.4%) are indicators of a positive shift.

With more positive matchups in their future, call me "Titans curious" for the next month.

Since Seattle is 2-0 with the second-best point differential (+27), I almost forgot they had a new play-caller. Because it's not like it's mattered for the overall WR3 in most drafts.

Jaxon Smith-Njigba was completely unguardable against Arizona.

9 REC, 155 YDS, 3 TD https://t.co/XuFwBIRfHm pic.twitter.com/TXm6lCG1it

Watching Jaxon Smith-Njigba is like that scene in Sherlock Holmes where Robert Downey Jr. explains ahead of time how he's going to beat a bare-knuckle boxer. You know it's coming, and the outcome is still a shock. And as JSN is the only WR with top-three marks in catches, yards and TDs, the "new Klint Kubiak," OC Brian Fleury, deserves some praise. That's especially true with Drew Lock starting in place of Sam Darnold.

But then there's also Jadarian Price's two-week output to consider.

whew look at how fast Jadarian Price can get north. https://t.co/5agGOW8Zue pic.twitter.com/9l2TdFxSD7

The good news is that Price looks the part of a Seahawks' RB. Fleury has built on Kubiak's use of outside-zone blocking schemes to provide rushing lanes, pushing Seattle's usage rate from 33.5% in '25 to 48.3% through two weeks. Undeniably, Price has the burst and power to get to the formation's boundary and up the field. But we haven't seen enough of him.

Rushing Rate: 50.0% (Week 1), 57.5% (Week 2)

Routes per Dropback: 26.0%, 32.5%

While Price took a backseat to Jeremiyah Love in college, a first-round RB does carry workload expectations. Sure, it's nice to see his usage ticking up, but he was still competing with George Holani and Emanuel Wilson for touches before getting hurt in Week 2. It's bad enough Zach Charbonnet may be practicing in the next couple of weeks. Coupled with a shared backfield right out of the gate, Price's opportunity level is the worst-case scenario. But he's shown he has the talent to change Fleury's mind.

Adj. Yards After Contact per Att.: 3.96, 8th (out of 39 qualifiers – min. 30% team rushing rate)

Forced Missed Tackle Rate: 30.4%, 7th

Explosive Run Rate: 13.0%, T-4th

Price's advanced metrics back up what we've seen on game day. And if you give any credence to PFF's charting, he's yet to allow a pressure or sack on pass-blocking snaps. In his only full game, he took 50% of the carries with a 40% route rate. With his shoulder injury not considered a lingering issue, Price becomes a buy-low candidate for those hunting for a low-end RB2.

title: Miami football legends honor Sean Taylor with heartfelt gesture
description: Emotions are high for the Hurricanes as the team celebrates 25 years since their 2001 BCS national championship.
fullText:
Sean Taylor will always be a part of one of the greatest college football teams ever. Miami football is enjoying a resurgence with Darian Mensah and Malachi Toney sparking national championship conversations.

However, the 2001 Miami Hurricanes are receiving lots of love recently as well. Adidas is recreating the BCS national title-winning team's iconic jerseys from 25 years ago.

Team legends like Clinton Portis, Ed Reed and Jeremy Shockey are helping relaunch the uniforms. Although, the trio's touching tribute for Taylor has Hurricanes fans emotional.

Current and former Miami players are taking part in the jersey release, and a promo shows Reed holding Taylor's iconic No. 26 jersey. Meanwhile, the group left a seat open for the former NFL star as another tribute.

MORE: Adidas celebrates Miami football with remake of iconic 2001 jerseys

Shoutout to Ed Reed, Clinton Portis and Jeremy Shockey for leaving the seat empty for Sean Taylor. You are loved and you missed dearly. #RIPSeanTaylor pic.twitter.com/TdRdSpIlXd

— Andrew (@98CanesFootball) September 23, 2026

Taylor tragically lost his life in Nov. 2007 during his fourth NFL season with the Washington Redskins (now the Washington Commanders). The two-time Pro Bowler was shot and killed in his Miami-area home.

The former top-five NFL Draft pick was considered one of the toughest defensive players in college and pro football history. Meanwhile, he played a massive role for Miami during the team's undefeated 2001 campaign.

Taylor earned All-American honors during his final collegiate season in 2003. He recorded an astounding 10 interceptions that year.

The Hurricanes' team was loaded with future NFL stars beyond just Portis, Reed and Taylor. Andre Johnson, Jonathan Vilma, Vince Wilfork and Frank Gore are just some of the talents that went on to have excellent NFL careers.

MORE: College football ACC power rankings entering Week 4

Miami's currently bringing back the team's iconic jerseys as one final tribute to the program before the school leaves Adidas for Nike in 2027. The Hurricanes signed a 10-year, $200 million deal with the highly-regarded sports apparel brand.

This season, Miami football is ranked sixth in the AP Top-25 while featuring two Heisman Trophy favorites in Mensah and Toney.

title: Jordan Love Loses Key Protector as Packers Starter Suffers Season-Ending Injury
description: The Green Bay Packers face an uphill battle after losing a crucial pillar of their offensive line for the remainder of the year. Zach Bako-Bewele suffered a devastating torn patellar tendon during Sunday’s hard-fought victory, completely reshaping the team’s upfront protection. With nine months of grueling recovery ahead, the front office must quickly pivot to […] The post Jordan Love Loses Key Protector as Packers Starter Suffers Season-Ending Injury appeared first on Gridiron Heroics.
fullText:
The Green Bay Packers face an uphill battle after losing a crucial pillar of their offensive line for the remainder of the year. Zach Bako-Bewele suffered a devastating torn patellar tendon during Sunday's hard-fought victory, completely reshaping the team's upfront protection.

With nine months of grueling recovery ahead, the front office must quickly pivot to keep championship aspirations alive. How head coach Matt LaFleur will now have to manage this crisis for quarterback protection moving forward.

Bako-Bewele suffered the injury during the first quarter of Green Bay's 20-17 overtime win over the New York Jets. He was blocking David Bailey when the patellar tendon in the same knee he injured last December against Denver fully tore.

NFL insider Ari Meirov broke the devastating news regarding the offensive line, reporting: "#Packers RT Zach Bako-Bewele (formerly Zach Tom) suffered a torn patellar tendon on Sunday and will miss the rest of the 2026 NFL season, he told reporters." The analyst further added, "A gut-punch loss for Green Bay's offensive line."

The 2022 fourth-round pick from Wake Forest has started 53 games, making his sudden absence a massive roster crisis for the franchise.

Green Bay already has Aaron Banks and Elgton Jenkins dealing with injuries. Anthony Belton is expected to take over at right tackle, but LaFleur also has to monitor Belton's elbow. The Packers now have fewer reliable options around Jordan Love at a time when their protection numbers are poor.

ESPN Analytics ranks Green Bay near the bottom of the league in pass-block win rate. Love is facing pressure in an average of 2.36 seconds after the snap, leaving little time for deeper routes to develop. The Packers finished last season 9-7-1 and still carried hopes of chasing another Lombardi Trophy, but the line has become the first major barrier to that goal.

The injury has also reopened the memory of Bako-Bewele's partial patellar tendon tear against Denver last December. He now faces surgery and a nine-month recovery, so his short-term focus is rehabilitation instead of a quick return.

Fox Sports reported his blunt reaction to the setback: "I mean, I don't think the turf helped. Yeah, I don't know. Just something that happened, so I've just got to move forward."

Green Bay must decide whether Belton can handle the job or whether the front office needs outside help. The Packers have already been linked to a possible trade for offensive support. Love's next test comes Thursday against the Atlanta Falcons at Lambeau Field, where every early pressure will measure the cost of losing Bako-Bewele.

title: Dylan Larkin joins Red Wings practice for first time since trade request
description: Dylan Larkin, who requested a trade in the off-season, took part in his first Detroit Red Wings practice of the season after rehabbing an injury
fullText:
Dylan Larkin took part in a Detroit Red Wings practice for the first time this fall.

His participation on Wednesday, Sept. 23, came after missing the first four days and two preseason games nursing an upper-body injury.

Larkin, who requested a trade shortly after last season ended, was not on a regular line, indicating he is still rehabbing his injury. The Wings have two exhibition games left: Thursday against the Buffalo Sabres and Saturday against the Columbus Blue Jackets. Both games are at Little Caesars Arena.

Larkin had been skating on his own before joining his teammates. He arrived at camp last week and met with reporters on Sept. 17, though he didn't shed much, if any, light on his future with the team.

GAME TIME: Red Wings young players devour Penguins in NHL preseason feast

Larkin would not answer when asked if his request to be traded still stands, or if there's a chance of reconciliation with his hometown NHL team, which drafted him at No. 15 in 2014.

It was a stunning bit of news, especially as Larkin was the captain (that has since been stripped from him) and has five years left on a deal with a very amenable $8.7 million salary cap hit. He also has a no-trade clause, which led him to limit his initial list of desired destinations to the Floria Panthers, Minnesota Wild and Vegas Golden Knights.

Larkin plays an important role for the Wings, centering their top line and headlining a position at which they lack depth. That, combined with the term left on his contract, made a trade for future assets unviable, as it would be a setback for the team's attempts to emerge from what last spring became 10 straight years of missing the playoffs.

The matter wasn't helped by the team separating from Steve Yzerman in his role as general manager in mid-July, and then not naming an interim GM − ultimately Shawn Horcoff − until two days before camp starts. But Horcoff was emphatic he won't change course, saying "a rebuild is out of the question."

Larkin would not answer why he made the request, what triggered the timing, questions about his list of destinations, or anything else other than to say he had discussed the matter with his teammates and the coaching staff and is focused on regaining their trust.

Contact Helene St. James at Hstjames@freepress.com.

fullText:
The Pentagon is altering the promotion process to get to the rank of general in an effort to “cut bureaucracy and demand true meritocracy” across the senior ranks, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth announced Tuesday.

In a video posted to social media, Hegseth declared the Defense Department this year will roll out the Joint Warfighter Evaluation, a new battlefield-style assessment for eligible colonels and Navy captains. The evaluation is intended to screen the officers aimed for one-star general or admiral on “their ability to fight, adapt, and win,” according to Hegseth.

“While the backbone of our military is our NCOs [noncommissioned officers] and our petty officers, victory depends on the commanders who lead them,” Hegseth said in the video.

“America needs warfighters who can master a chaotic battle space,” he added, later noting that commanders should be chosen by “proven competence, not paper credential.”

He likened the new evaluation to the Louisiana Maneuvers — a mass series of military exercises done directly before the U.S. entered World War II, during which roughly 400,000 troops conducted a wargame to evaluate America’s training, logistics and commanders.

Hegseth said such testing brought out leaders like former President Eisenhower, a five-star Army general who planned and carried out the Allied assault on the coast of Normandy and the liberation of Western Europe; Army Gen. Omar Bradley, the first chair of the Joint Chiefs of Staff who eventually oversaw the U.S. military’s policymaking in the Korean War; and Adm. Chester Nimitz, who commanded Allied air, land and sea in the Pacific theater during World War II.

The Joint Warfighter Evaluation “brings that standard to the modern multi-domain fight,” Hegseth said. “This evaluation is an objective equalizer. The scenario only cares about operational decisions under pressure.”

Hegseth said he had tasked Stuart Scheller, the deputy chief of staff to the undersecretary of Defense for personnel and readiness, to lead the effort a year ago.

Each military branch will have its own version of the evaluation, according to internal documents obtained by The Hill.

The Army will use a written assessment then a digital wargame; the Air Force and Space Force will require a two-hour online analysis test followed by a one-hour interactive simulation; the Navy will have officers travel to the Naval War College for a three-hour written assessment then a two-to-three-hour wargame; and the Marine Corps requires an eight-hour remote evaluation on an AI-enabled platform combining written assessments and situational judgment tests, according to an internal memo.

The Joint Staff will evaluate 50 to 60 Joint Forces Staff College students using a “hybrid” model with an independent written analysis followed by an “in-person, AI enabled execution phase” at Norfolk, Va. school, the memo said.

The current system has promotion boards that consider officers via their accumulated evaluations from their superiors throughout their careers.

The service will provide weekly updates on its pilot program development and implementation of the JWT Operational Planning Team (OPT) that will be coordinated with Scheller, Anthony Tata, the Pentagon’s Under Secretary of Defense for Personnel and Readiness, said in an Aug. 12 internal memo reviewed by The Hill.

Hegseth, a former Fox News host who served in the Army National Guard, has notoriously had an issue with the military’s promotion system, blocking numerous Army, Navy and Air Force promotions to one-star general or admirals — a large quantity of them Black and female service members.

The Pentagon chief has prioritized what he calls the “warrior ethos,” pushing the armed services to embrace higher physical standards and criticizing the military branches for promoting individuals based on what he has claimed, without proof, are race and gender quotas.

“Real toxic leadership is endangering subordinates with low standards. Real toxic leadership is promoting people based on immutable characteristics or quotas instead of based on merit,” Hegseth told senior military leaders last year in Quantico, Va.

title: Trump lawyers defend president banning journalists from White House ahead of court hearing – live
description: Trump lawyers say White House access is ‘a privilege, not a right’; CNN, Politico and MS Now to present case in court after president banned outlets from White House...
fullText:
In a new legal filing in the case over a trio of new outlets barred entry to the White House, Trump administration lawyers repeatedly defended the president’s ban by saying journalists were not entitled to access to the building.

“Access to the White House is a privilege, not a right,” the filing stated.

The filing went on to assert that the three outlets – by publishing sensitive or classified information obtained through its reporting – constituted a national security threat, giving the president the right to ax their credentials.

Trump banned the three outlets – CNN, MS Now, and Politico – last Friday in a snap decision announced via social media. He branded the three outlets “fake news” and threatened future bans against other outlets could follow.

Early the following week, the three publications filed a joint lawsuit asking a federal judge to restore their access, alleging that the action was an illegal act of retaliation that violated their First Amendment rights. A president, they argued in their complaint, can’t bar access to journalists based on reporting he doesn’t like.

Since then, Trump has found himself in an escalating tit-for-tat with the press, which has responded to the ban with measures of solidarity. Several outlets have declined to publish any images or video of the president so long as the three outlets are denied access to the White House. And the members of Trump’s standard TV pool – five channels, including CNN, who take turns traveling with the president, filming his daily activities, and distributing that footage – have ceased their duties.

title: Why fans are digging their claws into Wolverine over its patronising gameplay
description:
From highlighted ledges to characters telling you what to do, blockbuster games are increasingly taking the challenge out of playing – and players are pushing back
• Don’t get Pushing Buttons delivered to your inbox? Sign up here
Marvel’s Wolverine, the latest action game from Sony’s stable of expensive blockbuster-factory studios, has had an unfortunate launch. Reviews were decent, if not stellar, but a series of viral video clips from reviewers and streamers have made it the scapegoat for a patronising flavour of game design that gamers have hated for decades. This clip, from Skill Up’s review, shows the player entering a beautiful wintry landscape before being overwhelmed by visual cues telling them what they’re supposed to be doing there. Sonar pulses point you in the direction of objectives.
fullText:
From highlighted ledges to characters telling you what to do, blockbuster games are increasingly taking the challenge out of playing – and players are pushing back

Don’t get Pushing Buttons delivered to your inbox? 
Marvel’s Wolverine, the latest action game from Sony’s stable of expensive blockbuster-factory studios, has had an unfortunate launch. Reviews were decent, if not stellar, but a series of viral video clips from reviewers and streamers have made it the scapegoat for a patronising flavour of game design that gamers have hated for decades. This clip, from Skill Up’s review, shows the player entering a beautiful wintry landscape before being overwhelmed by visual cues telling them what they’re supposed to be doing there. Sonar pulses point you in the direction of objectives. Targets – which, it bears emphasising, are shaped like targets – get an extra reflective visual effect so you know you’re supposed to pay attention to them. A trail shows you not just where to go, but where the level’s sole hidden collectible is.

It is hand-holding to the point of parody. Indeed, it reminded me of the sniggersome Mario in Unreal Engine satirical videos that makes the social media rounds every few months (“A mushroom? I should take a look at this”). Skill Up’s clip has been followed by hundreds of others, gleefully ripping into Wolverine with ironic savagery. In one much-copied clip, a streamer simply lays down his controller during a motorbike chase sequence and watches as Wolverine speeds on regardless, bouncing off the scenery as the game plays itself.

People really detest this kind of thing. It’s impossible to pinpoint exactly when big-budget games started assuming that players were irredeemably stupid, but throughout the late 00s and 2010s it became more and more common to see obvious GPS trails showing you where to go, and for characters to talk to themselves to remind you what to do. At the same time, there’s been a cyclical discussion over the difficulty of games: every time a notably challenging game comes out, we rehash the same talking points about whether all games should have easy modes. Is it acceptable for games to shut players out if they aren’t prepared to “git gud”?

I am not a game designer, but as a critic who loves challenging games and has thought a lot about them, for me there is a difference between a game’s difficulty and its friction. A game might be difficult for all kinds of reasons, intentional or otherwise: perhaps the controls or camera aren’t great; perhaps there’s a mid-game boss with a bafflingly massive health bar and one devastating unblockable attack; perhaps the balancing is off. But a game’s friction is always an intentional part of its design. Friction is about how much a game helps you achieve its tasks. Games with perfect friction are clear about showing you what to do, but not overbearing about helping you do it: there is intentional distance, distance that you must broach with agency, strategy and skill. Friction leaves space for frustration and learning, and a sense of achievement.

A lot of modern blockbuster game design seems hellbent on removing this friction. Not sure where to go? Here – follow this brightly coloured trail of fart gas. Not sure how to climb that building? We’ve helpfully painted the ledges yellow. Have you stood still for 30 seconds? We’ll have another character talk in your ear and tell you exactly what you need to do. Playing through the opening hours of 007 First Light recently, I was dismayed when Bond inevitably acquired a watch that magically highlights important things in his vicinity with the press of a button.

At its best, game design like this helps players avoid becoming irrevocably stuck. At its worst, it totally removes agency and challenge – you know, the reasons that many of us play games in the first place. Fundamentally, a game is only fun if you have to do something. I don’t play games for passive entertainment. That’s what binge-watching Netflix is for. If you don’t have to invest anything to reap the rewards, the experience just washes over you.

Games can be difficult and have high friction. In Hollow Knight: Silksong, you are constantly figuring out what to do, where the next boss might be, how to open that tantalisingly blocked path. Achieving those goals is then also very challenging, requiring practice and mastery of whip-fast fighting and precise jumping. Or they can be high-friction, low-difficulty: Blue Prince tells you literally nothing about how to make your way to its mansion’s secret 46th room, but it’s not difficult to walk around and try out ideas. An example of a low-friction, high-difficulty game, meanwhile, would be a combat-focused one like Devil May Cry (or most shooters), where the aim is always “kill all the guys to open the next area” but actually killing all those guys is majorly demanding.

Low-friction, low-difficulty games hold very little interest. Many mobile games fall into this category, where you barely have to do anything save prod the screen to provoke a dopamine-shower of flashy visual effects (I’m looking at you, Monopoly Go). It’s unfair to lump Wolverine in with these almost entirely valueless games – but it is instructive that it has been subjected to such ridicule.

The infamously challenging Dark Souls, a dramatically influential game that turned 15 years old this week, seemed to remind the entire games industry that you can actually trust players: that they won’t drop the controller and storm off as soon as they get skewered by a skeleton. That there’s immense and unique pleasure in participating in a game, unravelling it, conquering it little by little with skill and understanding. I hope that the reaction to Wolverine will serve as another reminder of that fact, for any executives who need to hear it.

Konami’s horror series is on a roll lately. The Silent Hill 2 remake was very well received (with a few exceptions, including our critic), last year’s feminist, small-town Japanese horror story Silent Hill: f was excellent, and now Silent Hill: Townfall has succeeded in sending the series to a new setting: an island off the Scottish coast. Per our reviewer Lewis Gordon: “This is a taut, smart tale, less about psychosexual terror than psychosocial dread… Townfall seems to understand that some things should remain shrouded in fog. The fate of St Amelia naturally festers in our imagination. How very Silent Hill.”

Available on: PS5, Xbox, PC

 Estimated playtime: 12-15 hours

Pikachu is now an astronaut, thanks to a collaboration between Pokémon and the European Space Agency as part of the franchise’s seemingly endless series of 30th birthday celebrations. Human astronaut Sophie Adenaut brought a Pikachu plush up to the International Space Station, where it spent 67 days in orbit.

According to Sonic Team boss Takashi Iizuka, Sega was once poised to kill off the whole Sonic franchise. It was the success of 2020’s live-action Sonic movie that saved it. “I had to fight within the organization to keep the franchise as long as possible,” he told One More Game.

The new Resident Evil movie is out, and it’s going down well. Aftermath describes it as like watching your inept stoner roommate play the games; certified horror-game enjoyer Keith Stuart says it’s one of the best video game adaptations he’s seen.

The Tokyo Game Show had to wrap up one day early last week due to an incoming typhoon. Gamesindustry.biz has a slightly depressing rundown of the show, which was heavily dominated by AI.

There have been yet more dramatic changes at Microsoft’s Xbox division. The company is all but closing Halo Studios and moving Halo’s development to Activision, which will also now be in charge of storied British studio Rare. Multi-BAFTA-winning studio Ninja Theory is starting consultations on a proposed closure, having failed to find a funding deal to return itself to independence.

Silent Hill: Townfall – shame and suffering on the Scottish coast | ★★★★☆

Resident Evil – Zach Cregger’s rebooted action horror is a wild rollercoaster ride | ★★★★☆

Control Resonant – save New York from paranormal phenomena | ★★★☆☆

Roman Sands RE:Build – marooned in a crumbling vaporwave dream | ★★★☆☆

Reader Mike asks: “I just finished reading your article about the GameCube, which ironically got me thinking about the PS1 & 2, marvellous machines which I remember fondly. The game I got bundled with my PS2 was ‘Shadow of Memories’ which sticks with me to this day, the story was magnificent and also beautifully rendered, with multiple endings. Are there any similar ‘timeywimey’ games set in beautiful European villages, evoking memories of this game, out there today? Either on Android or PS5?”

This question unearthed a bunch of half-remembered fragments from the early days of the PS2 – I definitely played Shadow of Memories as well. It’s a Konami game about a young German travelling through time, trying to solve his own murder. You mentioned games available on PS5, so here are a few that have some of the same elements. The Life is Strange series is set in the US but has a similar time-travel and murder-solving premise; Clair Obscur is a very different kind of game but is as uniquely and surreally European; this year’s Japanese RPG The Adventures of Elliot involves travelling through different eras to prevent a catastrophe. None of these have the same strange adventure-game atmosphere as Shadow of Memories, though – that’s something that felt really specific to the PS2 era. Readers, have you any more suggestions for Mike?

If you have a question for Question Block – or anything else to say about the newsletter – email us at pushingbuttons@theguardian.com.

title: El Niño predicted to cause nearly half a million more deaths
description:
